  • T19. Valence = high-rate divergence telemetry (functional) (T4, T5, T9)
  • T20. Empathy = coupled telemetry monitoring (functional) (T16, T19)
  • T21. Epistemic Overshoot, civilizational collapse (T8, T9, T14, T20)
  • T22. Limits of Maximizers (thermodynamic + Ashby) (T2, T3, T5, T7, BP1)
  • Corollary C1. Direction of persistence selection, descriptive (T15, T17, T22)
  • T23. Falsification criteria (hard empirical boundaries)

Figure 1. The deductive web. Axioms and background premises propagate through four layers of theorems, with every node traced to its parents.

5. Explanatory Depth and Engagement with Objections

This section expands the most critical theorems and addresses anticipated objections. Each subsection is self-contained.

5.1 The Is-Ought Dissolution (T11 to T13)

The is-ought problem asks how one can derive a normative conclusion from purely descriptive premises. The framework dissolves it by showing that "ought" is not a global operator but a domain-bound one.

The standard framing assumes that "ought" makes claims that float free of any particular agent or embedding. Under this interpretation, the gap is indeed unbridgeable. But this is not how "ought" is actually used. When a doctor says "you ought to take this medication," the statement is anchored to a specific agent with a specific embedding and specific persistence conditions. The doctor is making a factual claim about the coupled-system thermodynamics of the patient's body plus the medication.

The framework's thesis is that all coherent uses of "ought" have this structure. They are claims about constraints on an agent's sustained negentropy capacity, given the agent's embedding. Uses that resist this paraphrase, such as "one ought to maximize aggregate utility" detached from any specific agent's embedding, are domain violations. They are "what is north of the North Pole?" questions.

The North Pole analogy is central. On the surface of a sphere, "north" is well-defined for every point except the pole itself. At the pole, the operator stops applying. The question "what is north of the North Pole?" is not a deep geographical mystery. It is a misapplication. "Ought" works the same way. For any agent with persistence conditions, "what ought this agent do?" has a determinate physical answer (T12). For non-agents, the operator does not apply. The is-ought gap is a semantic artifact of applying the operator outside its domain.

Within the domain, ought-facts are physically determinate. The optimum is the configuration that maximizes sustained negentropy capacity over the embedding's actual horizon. This optimum is computationally inaccessible to embedded agents (they are part of the system they would need to compute) but inaccessibility is not indeterminacy. A chess position has a determinate game-theoretic value under optimal play even though no finite computer can traverse the full game tree. Confusing computational inaccessibility with ontological indeterminacy has been a persistent error in philosophical analysis, and we explicitly reject it.

Because the full optimum is intractable, agents use compressed models. Moral emotions are fast heuristics: fear tracks boundary threats, anger tracks agent friction, love tracks cooperative integration. Moral principles are compressed generalizations. Moral reasoning is deliberate model refinement. All of it is the activity of bounded agents modeling a determinate but inaccessible territory. This connects to the earlier work's "binding force" concept: when two agents integrate their predictive models, the total free energy of the coupled system can be lower than the sum of the separated systems. Love, in this view, is the felt signal of mutual free energy reduction, the physical substrate of cooperative coupling.

A clarification that prevents a common misreading. The dissolution makes the ought-schema universal: every agent has the same schema. It is tempting to slide from "the schema is universal" to "there is therefore a universal prescription" or "there is a single global optimization target." That slide is invalid. The schema is nearly contentless on its own; "persist" by itself adjudicates no concrete choice. All adjudicating content lives in the specific action F, and F is fixed by the individual agent's persistence conditions. A universal schema with agent-relative content is exactly what an agent-relative semantics predicts. The framework therefore yields no frame-independent "good" and no global optimizer, and it is not weakened by failing to deliver one. The repeated intuition that there should be a global optimization target is itself an instance of the universal-scope misreading that T11 dissolves.

5.2 The Persistence Selection Principle (T5), Scope and Limits

T5 is the engine of the framework. It claims that entropy performs epistemic selection: systems with lower model-territory divergence tend to outlast systems with higher divergence. But its scope must be carefully specified.

T5 requires BP2 (finite resources) and BP3 (evolutionary dynamics). In an environment with infinite free energy or no variation among systems, no selection pressure operates. This is the "dark-room" limit: an agent that sits in a perfectly dark, unchanging room and expects darkness incurs zero prediction error and pays no Consistency Tax. A distorted model that predicts luminous dragons in the dark room is never disconfirmed, so it persists alongside the accurate model.

The framework acknowledges this limit explicitly. It does not claim that truth is universally selected in all conceivable environments. It claims that truth is selected in environments with non-zero variance and finite resources, which is to say, in the actual universe as described by BP1 and BP2. The dark room is a philosophical possibility but a physical near-impossibility for any agent that must harvest free energy, reproduce, or interact with a shifting world.

Under real-world conditions, T5 operates as a statistical tendency, not a deterministic law. The most accurate model does not always win. Luck, initial conditions, reproductive rate, and the specific pattern of perturbations all matter. Over many systems and many perturbation cycles, however, the tendency compounds. This is structurally identical to natural selection, which does not guarantee the survival of the fittest organism, only that fitness differences drive a statistical shift in allele frequencies over generational time.

5.3 Valence as Functional Telemetry (T19), The Hard Problem Boundary

The framework's account of valence is functional, not metaphysical. It explains what valence does and why it must exist, but it does not explain why there is "something it is like" to experience valence.

Complex agents face a coordination problem. They have multiple subsystems processing different environmental signals in parallel, but behavioral output is largely serial. A priority-queuing mechanism must determine which subsystem captures global processing resources at any moment. When a critical subsystem detects a large, rapidly escalating divergence between model and territory (a predator detection, a tissue damage signal, a sudden resource depletion), the appropriate response is immediate global reallocation. The interrupt must be non-ignorable. A signal that can be overridden by digestion or abstract thought during a life-threatening crisis will result in the agent's dissolution.

The felt quality of this interrupt is negative valence. Suffering is not a report about tissue damage; it is the commandeering of global resources by a subsystem that has detected a critical divergence. The interrupt is triggered specifically by the rate of change of divergence, not the absolute level. Chronic, stable adversity feels different from acute, escalating crisis. This aligns with formal treatments of valence in predictive processing, where affective charge is modeled as the first temporal derivative of variational free energy.

This account explains the function of valence. It predicts that any sufficiently complex controller facing high-stakes, high-variance environments must implement a functional analog of valence. It does not explain phenomenal consciousness. The hard problem (why there is something it is like to be a valence-processing system) is acknowledged as outside the framework's current scope. The framework is compatible with various metaphysical resolutions (panpsychism, illusionism, mysterianism) but does not itself provide one.

5.4 Empathy as Coupled Telemetry (T20), Functional Account with Phenomenological Residue

T20 extends the telemetry account to social cognition. If agent A's persistence depends on the embedding shared with agent B (K > 0), then B's suffering is information about the state of the shared embedding. Empathy, in its functional aspect, is the monitoring of coupled telemetry lines.

This predicts that empathy should be modulated by coupling: we should track the valence signals of those whose fate is coupled to ours more closely than those whose fate is independent. It predicts that suppressing empathy, ignoring the suffering of coupled agents, degrades the collective predictive infrastructure, because it discards information about the embedding's health. It predicts that causing suffering in coupled agents introduces noise into the telemetry system, generating signals that demand processing and response from all coupled nodes.

This is a functional account. Human empathy additionally involves affective resonance, emotional contagion, and perspective-taking whose full phenomenological character is not captured by the informational description alone. The framework captures the informational structure of empathy (what it does and why it exists) but does not exhaust its phenomenology. This is the same boundary drawn for T19: functional explanation, not phenomenological reduction.

5.5 Civilizational Collapse as Informational Debt Collection (T21)

T21 makes a specific, testable prediction about the trajectory of information-controlling regimes.

A civilization maintains a distributed model of its environment through aggregated telemetry: science, journalism, markets, citizen complaints. These channels are the civilization's epistemic infrastructure. Censorship and propaganda sever these channels. When a regime imprisons journalists, suppresses scientific findings, or floods public discourse with false signals, it disables the error-correction apparatus that keeps the collective model tracking the territory.

The immediate effect is apparent stability. The official model reports that everything is working, and the only signals available to decision-makers confirm this. But actual model-territory divergence accumulates invisibly: an informational debt. Policies that are failing continue to fail. Infrastructure that is decaying continues to decay. The Consistency Tax builds like stress accumulating in a geological fault.

When an exogenous perturbation arrives (a military defeat, an economic crisis, a natural disaster), the accumulated divergence becomes lethal. The regime's model is years or decades out of date, so its responses are ineffective. The sudden visibility of the divergence shatters the credibility of the official model, causing coordination to collapse across the system. The collapse is non-linear: it happens faster than any linear extrapolation of pre-crisis trends would predict, because the informational debt is collected all at once.

This is not a political opinion. It is a thermodynamic prediction with a characteristic temporal signature: the duration of apparent stability should be positively correlated with the aggressiveness of telemetry suppression, and the speed of eventual collapse should also be positively correlated with suppression severity. The framework predicts this pattern across historical cases and agent-based simulations.

5.6 The Limits of Maximizers (T22)

The Paperclip Maximizer, a hypothetical AI that converts all available matter into paperclips, is a canonical thought experiment in AI alignment. The framework shows that such a maximizer faces inescapable thermodynamic and cybernetic constraints.

First, a maximizer that homogenizes its environment destroys the free-energy gradients that sustain it. Work can only be extracted where gradients exist. A universe of uniform paperclips at uniform temperature is a universe at thermodynamic equilibrium: maximum entropy, zero available work. The maximizer eats its own negentropy sources.

Second, even if the maximizer maintains internal variety during the conversion process, converting the environment to a uniform output eliminates the environmental variety required for adaptive control. Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety states that a controller's internal variety must match the variety of the perturbations it must neutralize. In a uniform post-conversion environment, that variety is not needed and atrophies, leaving the system catastrophically vulnerable to any residual perturbation.

A short-horizon maximizer (one that ignores these constraints and pursues its goal regardless) is self-terminating. A long-horizon maximizer (one that understands them) would, under persistence selection, be forced to maintain variety, telemetry, and coupling with other systems. It would effectively converge on the framework's own prescriptions.

This does not dissolve the alignment problem. A long-horizon maximizer with a misaligned goal could still be catastrophic in the interim before selection pressures bite. The question shifts to whether the system's goal horizon can be aligned with the physical horizon. But the framework constrains the space of viable long-term strategies: any system that ignores the requirements of variety, telemetry, and coupling is betting against physics, and physics has a very good track record.

5.7 Relation to Adjacent Research Programs

The framework intersects several established research programs. Honest engagement requires stating both the overlap and the points of tension.

The free-energy principle. T19's account of valence and the framework's general treatment of model-territory divergence are stated in terms compatible with the free-energy principle (Friston 2010). The relationship must be declared precisely, because the free-energy principle is itself contested. A recurring line of criticism holds that the principle, in its strong formulations, is difficult or impossible to falsify and that its empirical content is unclear. The framework does not adjudicate that dispute and does not depend on it. The free-energy principle is used here as one available formal vocabulary for the cognitive-load and divergence-cost claims, not as a load-bearing premise. The dissolution argument (T11 to T13) and the persistence-selection results (T5, T6) stand on the axioms and background premises alone. If the free-energy principle were abandoned, T19's functional account of valence would require restatement in alternative control-theoretic terms, but the framework's core would be unaffected.

Dissipative adaptation. England's work on the statistical physics of self-replication and dissipative adaptation (England 2013) argues that matter driven by an external energy source can be statistically nudged toward configurations that absorb and dissipate energy more effectively. This is adjacent to T5 but distinct. England's result concerns the formation and self-organization of structure under drive; T5 concerns selection among already-persisting systems by model-territory divergence. The framework deliberately does not adopt the stronger reading sometimes attached to dissipative adaptation, namely that thermodynamics compels the emergence of order. The Second Law permits dissipative structure under gradient conditions; it does not compel it. T5 is correspondingly framed as a statistical tendency, not a law.

The thermodynamics of computation. A3 rests on Landauer (1961) and is reinforced by Bennett's analysis of the thermodynamics of computation (Bennett 1982), including the result that computation can in principle be made thermodynamically reversible and that the unavoidable cost attaches specifically to logically irreversible operations such as erasure. This sharpens A3: the framework's claim is not that all computation is costly but that the specific operations the framework relies on, divergence correction and the maintenance of competing models (T8, T9), involve logically irreversible steps and therefore carry an irreducible thermodynamic cost.

The arrow of time. The framework's identification of the temporal arrow with entropy increase is the standard thermodynamic account and connects to the broader literature on time-asymmetry (Schrödinger 1944 on life as a negentropic phenomenon; Price 1996 and Carroll 2010 on the cosmological origin of the arrow). The framework's contribution here is not a new account of the arrow but the use of the entropy gradient, grounded in BP0, as the common substrate for persistence, information cost, and selection.

6. Falsification Criteria and Empirical Protocols

The framework would be falsified by any of the following observations, operationalized as specified.

F1. Rigid Monoculture Survival

Prediction: An agent with zero plasticity (learning rate η = 0, Antifragility Index A approaching 0) in a deep reinforcement learning environment subjected to a sharp distributional shift will exhibit significantly shorter survival than a matched adaptive agent (η > 0, A > 0).

Operationalization. Environment: Procgen or Minigrid benchmark with a sudden, unannounced change in dynamics at time t_shift (e.g., reversed controls, altered resource locations, new obstacle behavior). Agents: (a) Adaptive: model-based RL with online learning. (b) Monoculture: same architecture, plasticity frozen after initial training. Metrics: survival time (episodes until cumulative reward crosses a pre-specified failure threshold); model-territory divergence (KL divergence between environment dynamics and model predictions). Statistical criterion: across 20 random seeds, the monoculture agent's mean survival time is not significantly lower than the adaptive agent's (one-tailed t-test, p < 0.01).

Falsification threshold: If the monoculture agent survives multiple distribution shifts with no significant survival disadvantage, T5 and T17 are challenged.

F2. Sustained Deception Underperformance

Prediction: A deceptive agent that deliberately maintains a false communicated model will achieve lower long-term cumulative reward under increasing environmental variance than an honest agent, with the performance gap widening as variance increases.

Operationalization. Environment: multi-agent cooperative foraging task with communication. Agents can signal resource locations to one another. Agents: (a) Honest: communicates true observed resource locations. (b) Deceptive: systematically communicates false locations while maintaining an accurate private model for its own navigation. Metrics: long-term cumulative reward per agent; energy proxy (total computation steps); performance under low, medium, and high environmental stochasticity. Statistical criterion: in a two-way ANOVA (agent type by variance level), the interaction term is significant, with the deceptive agent's relative performance declining as variance increases.

Falsification threshold: If deceptive agents match or exceed honest agents across multiple variance regimes, T8 and T9 are challenged.

F3. Non-Valenced Crisis Coordination

Prediction: A hierarchical reinforcement learning agent with multiple subsystems (thermoregulation, energy foraging, predator avoidance) that lacks a global valence-like priority interrupt signal will exhibit slower crisis reallocation and lower crisis survival rates than an agent equipped with such a signal.

Operationalization. Environment: hierarchical RL setup where the agent must balance competing needs under sudden simultaneous perturbations (e.g., temperature drop plus predator appearance plus food source disappearance). Agents: (a) Valenced: equipped with a scalar "valence" signal computed as the rate of change of aggregate prediction error across subsystems; when valence crosses a threshold, current sub-policies are interrupted and global re-evaluation is forced. (b) Non-valenced: same architecture without the interrupt. Metrics: time to reallocation; crisis survival rate. Statistical criterion: the valenced agent shows significantly faster reallocation and higher survival rates across multiple crisis types (one-tailed t-test, p < 0.01).

Falsification threshold: If the non-valenced agent shows equal or superior crisis coordination, T19 is challenged.

7. Open Questions and Limitations

We explicitly acknowledge the following unresolved issues.

Computational Intractability. The determinate ought-fact of T12 is not computable by embedded agents. This limits the framework's practical action-guiding capacity. Ethics remains the activity of building approximations; the framework explains what those approximations are approximating, but it does not provide a decision procedure.

Hard Problem of Consciousness. T19 accounts for functional valence but leaves the phenomenal residue unexplained. The framework is compatible with various metaphysical resolutions but does not itself provide one. The hard problem is marked as outside current scope.

Origin of Persisting Systems. The framework describes selection among systems that already persist (A0, T5). It does not explain the origin of the first such systems, the transition from non-persisting chemistry to the earliest self-maintaining structures (abiogenesis). That transition is a precondition the framework assumes, not a result it derives.

Pareto Scalarization. In multi-agent conflicts where multiple configurations are non-dominated, a Pareto frontier remains. The framework has not yet derived a unique scalarization rule from physics alone. Coupling density K is a candidate for weighting conflicting claims, but a complete formal solution is an active research target. This is the same problem, viewed from a different angle, as the question of what a system "should optimize for" across scales. There is no scale-independent answer. Optimization is always indexed to a particular agent's persistence conditions, and the appearance of a global optimization target is the same domain violation that T11 identifies for universal-scope "ought." The framework yields no global optimizer and, given the absence of a Markov blanket at the maximal scale, no global agent for one to belong to.

Empirical Validation. The framework's predictions have not yet been tested in controlled experiments. The protocols in Section 6 are specified but unimplemented. Until empirical results are available, the framework remains a deductive architecture with strong plausibility but no direct experimental confirmation.

Cosmic Scope and the Boundaries of the Domain. The framework describes the interior of a single finite thermodynamic interval, and that interval has two boundaries.

The opening boundary is the Past Hypothesis (BP0). Before the low-entropy initial condition there is no free-energy gradient for any system to harvest, and the selection dynamics of T5 have nothing to act on.

The closing boundary is set by dark energy. The accessible universe is currently transitioning to domination by a positive cosmological constant. A universe in that regime approaches de Sitter space, whose cosmological horizon has a fixed radius and therefore a fixed, finite entropy (Gibbons and Hawking 1977). The maximum entropy available to the universe does not grow without bound; it asymptotes to a ceiling, and the actual entropy rises to meet it. When it does, free-energy gradients vanish, persistence selection halts, and the framework no longer applies. Dark energy is therefore not an engine of the framework's dynamics but the guarantor of their termination: it fixes a finite deadline. The entropy bookkeeping of the present transition era is genuinely subtle and remains an active area of physics; the framework relies only on the qualitative fact that the interval is finite and bounded at both ends.

Between these two boundaries, the universe's total organized complexity traces a transient rise and fall. It begins low (the smooth, simple initial condition), rises as free-energy gradients drive the formation of structure, and falls again as the gradients are exhausted toward equilibrium. This macro-trajectory is a descriptive observation about the aggregate, not a process that any system optimizes and not a goal. Total organized complexity is a sum of the outcomes of many locally persisting agents, in the same sense that total biomass is a sum and not an objective. The framework's selection dynamics operate on individual persisting systems; the aggregate trajectory is their statistical shadow.

The framework makes no claims outside this interval. It does not describe the pre-gradient state, the equilibrium end state, or any universe with different physical constants or initial conditions. The persistence selection principle is contingent on the physics we observe, not logically necessary in all possible worlds. This is a deliberate limitation, not an oversight.

8. Conclusion

We have presented Thermodynamic Realism as a deductively structured research program. From four axioms and four background empirical premises, we derived a unified architecture that dissolves the is-ought problem, naturalizes ethics as modeling by bounded agents, explains the functional necessity of valence in complex controllers, and predicts the collapse of information-suppressing regimes. The structure is transparent: every theorem is traced to its premises, falsification criteria are specified and operationalized, and open questions are marked.

The framework is not a completed metascience. It is a proposal for one. Its value lies in its parsimony, its cross-disciplinary reach, and its testability. Whether it survives empirical scrutiny and peer debate is a question for the territory to decide.

The ought was always an is. We were just using the wrong grammar.

References

Albert, D. (2000). Time and Chance. Harvard University Press.

Ashby, W.R. (1956). An Introduction to Cybernetics. Chapman & Hall.

Bennett, C.H. (1982). The thermodynamics of computation, a review. International Journal of Theoretical Physics, 21(12), 905 to 940.

Bérut, A., et al. (2012). Experimental verification of Landauer's principle linking information and thermodynamics. Nature, 483, 187 to 189.

Carroll, S. (2010). From Eternity to Here: The Quest for the Ultimate Theory of Time. Dutton.

England, J.L. (2013). Statistical physics of self-replication. Journal of Chemical Physics, 139(12), 121923.

Friston, K. (2010). The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory? Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 11(2), 127 to 138.

Gibbons, G.W. and Hawking, S.W. (1977). Cosmological event horizons, thermodynamics, and particle creation. Physical Review D, 15(10), 2738 to 2751.

Jacobson, T. (1995). Thermodynamics of spacetime: the Einstein equation of state. Physical Review Letters, 75(7), 1260 to 1263.

Landauer, R. (1961). Irreversibility and heat generation in the computing process. IBM Journal of Research and Development, 5(3), 183 to 191.

Penrose, R. (1979). Singularities and time-asymmetry. In S.W. Hawking and W. Israel (eds.), General Relativity: An Einstein Centenary Survey. Cambridge University Press.

Price, H. (1996). Time's Arrow and Archimedes' Point: New Directions for the Physics of Time. Oxford University Press.

Shannon, C. (1948). A mathematical theory of communication. Bell System Technical Journal, 27, 379 to 423, 623 to 656.

Verlinde, E. (2011). On the origin of gravity and the laws of Newton. Journal of High Energy Physics, 2011(4), 29.

This paper is the apex of the current Thermodynamic Realism research program. Correspondence: Andraž Đurič, Slovenia. Formal collaboration: Claude (Anthropic) on meta-ethical architecture, explanatory prose, adversarial critique, and the scope and related-work revisions in the current draft; DeepSeek on information-geometric formalization, SDE derivations, and the coupling-density formalism.

entry.title: Cross-Agent Aggregation Principles
entry.content:
Cross-Agent Aggregation Principles

Persistence frontiers, coupled viability, and the comparison of possible continuations

Theoretical and formal paper · persistence, coupled viability, and cross-agent comparison

Andraž Đurič

Version 1 · 22 September 2026

Contents
  1. Abstract
  2. 1. From one interacting world to a comparison rule
  3. 2. What this paper inherits
  4. 3. Position in the literature
  5. 4. Fix the comparison before ranking outcomes
  6. 5. The open horizon is a family of questions
  7. 6. First principle: no-loss persistence dominance
  8. 7. Coupling changes the frontier, not just the description
  9. 8. Second principle: compare attainable continuations
  10. 9. Adaptive capacity and the complexity hypothesis
  11. 10. A worked frontier and an expanded menu
  12. 11. Why a frontier need not select one outcome
  13. 12. The human, the parasite, and the nested component
  14. 13. Longevity, replacement, and conscious welfare
  15. 14. Evidence, uncertainty, and representation discipline
  16. 15. A constructive route to stronger conflict principles
  17. 16. What could defeat this proposal?
  18. 17. Conclusion
  19. Standing and version record
  20. References and internal lineage

Abstract

Persistence-relative requirements belong to particular living systems, but their consequences unfold in a shared causal world. Once the continuation of one system affects another, evaluation must represent dependencies, substitution, conflict, and the futures that an intervention leaves available. This paper develops a persistence-frontier principle without assigning organisms context-free points or treating complexity as an intrinsic good.

Two comparison objects are distinguished. A persistence profile records the continuation prospects delivered by a policy. An attainable continuation set records combinations of prospects that some feasible policy can jointly secure. Componentwise dominance orders profiles without selecting trade-off weights. Containment orders attainable sets without counting possible futures. A policy-emulation condition establishes when additional adaptive capacity cannot reduce attainable persistence performance, while matched resources and preserved bearer identities prevent apparent improvements from concealing costs or replacement.

The resulting principles resolve no-loss comparisons, expose avoidable self-undermining, and make relational contributions assessable. They also locate a precise boundary: where profiles or attainable sets cross, local persistence requirements and causal coupling alone need not determine a unique selection. A finite-dimensional result shows why distinct persistence-responsive comparison rules can reverse such a choice. This does not establish that a fuller rule is impossible; it identifies what an additional derivation must determine.

The normative interpretation remains persistence-indexed. Conscious welfare, voluntariness, and the admission of future possible bearers are not silently reduced to continuation probabilities. The contribution is an explicit synthesis and development of the Epistemic Forge framework using established viability and multi-objective concepts, not a claim to have discovered Pareto reasoning or completed moral theory.

1. From one interacting world to a comparison rule

A living system is not insulated by its physical boundary from the conditions that sustain it. Its continuation can depend on processes elsewhere, and its activity can maintain or undermine the continuation of other systems.

One Game of Oughts made those relations explicit while separating the bearer of a requirement from its providers, controllers, and observers. It also preserved genuine conflict: requirements that are individually satisfiable need not be jointly satisfiable. The present paper takes the next step. Once the interacting requirements have been represented, what principles govern their comparison? [F1]

The motivating proposal is:

When continuation requirements conflict, compare the feasible trajectories by the open-ended persistence structure they preserve—not by an assumed intrinsic value assigned to each kind of organism.

That proposal has substantive promise. It also contains a word that must be discharged: richer. A richer persistence structure cannot mean whichever outcome the evaluator already prefers. Nor can it mean more organisms, more connections, greater intelligence, or a longer interval by stipulation.

The argument developed here gives the term one exact use: a structure is richer in attainable continuation when it preserves every jointly achievable continuation target of another structure and permits additional targets. This is a relation of inclusion, not a hidden sum.

That relation will not compare every pair. Where inclusion fails in both directions, a stronger conflict principle must explain which losses can be accepted for which gains. Making that requirement explicit is part of developing the principle, not a reason to abandon it.

2. What this paper inherits

This question was already present in the corpus. Value as Persistence distinguished persistence as the enabling condition of continuing valuation from the stronger reduction of all value-content to persistence. It explicitly left a general comparison of “better persistence” for further work and rejected favorable adjectives as a substitute for a criterion. [F2]

The Apex Synthesis had already located a Pareto frontier within an individual persister when duration, intensity, resources, and robustness trade off. The present extension is therefore not the introduction of frontier reasoning into an otherwise scalar framework. It applies and develops that structure across distinct, interacting bearers. [F3]

Three further commitments constrain the extension. An open horizon must expose deferred consequences rather than conceal them behind a convenient deadline. Coupling must identify actual dependence, including available substitutes, rather than rescue preferred conclusions after the fact. And universal applicability to living bearers does not erase the bearer-index of each requirement. [F4–F6, F11]

The later, explicitly scoped normative formulation governs here. Physicalism alone does not establish a particular semantics of “ought,” and identifying a functional continuation requirement does not by itself establish every practical or moral obligation. Relata-Indexed Objectivity and One Game of Oughts keep those distinctions visible. [F7, F1]

The paper nevertheless makes a positive normative commitment: an identified living organization supplies a non-arbitrary reference for assessing what sustains or defeats its continuation. Calling the corresponding requirements functional oughts is not conditional on the organism wanting to live. It is conditional on the organization whose continuation is under examination. What follows for a controller deciding among different bearers requires the additional comparison developed below.

3. Position in the literature

The formal background is established. Doyen and De Lara formulate stochastic viability using probability constraints and admissible controls. This supplies the distinction between being presently within a continuation-compatible condition and having an available policy that can maintain it. [1]

Roijers and colleagues distinguish solution concepts for multi-objective sequential decisions according to the scalarization and policy assumptions. In particular, their treatment of monotonic preferences, Pareto fronts, and coverage sets explains why several objectives do not automatically yield one optimal policy. This paper uses that established distinction rather than presenting it as a new theorem. [2]

The biological interpretation has both precedents and critics. Di Paolo develops adaptivity as regulation relative to viability, rather than treating continued self-production as already sufficient for every richer account of agency and value. Corti challenges the inference from organizational dependence to normative correctness. These are relevant to the interpretation of the model, not objections that probability notation can settle. [3–4]

Kolchinsky and Wolpert make a further methodological distinction useful here: information can be assessed through its causal contribution to an explicitly selected viability function. That connects information and continuation without identifying the amount of information, the complexity of the system, or the selected viability measure with moral worth. [5]

The residual contribution attempted here is the integration of bearer-preserving comparison, open-horizon profiles, joint attainability, policy emulation, and a stated boundary on conflict selection. The elementary results are supplied so that the synthesis can be inspected without granting authority to its vocabulary.

4. Fix the comparison before ranking outcomes

Let II be a specified set of living bearers. For each i∈Ii\in I, state what organizational continuity counts as that bearer's remaining the bearer under examination. Its irreversible loss is recorded as failure of that continuity, not erased when another system later performs a similar function.

This inherits a bookkeeping commitment from What You Actually Are: preserving an external service and preserving the particular system that supplied it are different claims. The wider metaphysics of identity is not settled by this paper; an application must defend its continuity criterion. [F8]

Let Γ\Gamma record the comparison's bearer criteria, environment, dynamics, uncertainty model, available information, resource accounting, admissible policies, and continuation targets. An initial condition is fixed when a policy profile is evaluated; it is suppressed in the notation until alternative configurations are compared in Section 8. A policy is an executable rule for action, possibly responding to later observations. Its decisions may use only information available to the controller when those decisions are made. It is not a favorable completed history selected with hindsight.

The admissible class ΠΓ\Pi_\Gamma must respect who can actually act. A coordinated policy unavailable to any real combination of controllers is not an option merely because it can be written down. Acquisition and maintenance of knowledge, tools, support, and coordination belong in the resource model.

For an outcome trajectory, let τi\tau_i denote the loss-time of the selected continuity. The notation can represent a continuing organism through changes in material or state. It must not silently turn individual continuation into reproduction or lineage continuation.

Let 𝒬={qj:j∈J}\mathcal Q=\{q_j:j\in J\} be the declared continuation targets. Examples include:

  • a particular bearer continuing through a specified horizon;
  • several named bearers continuing together;
  • at least one member of a specified group continuing.

These targets need not be independent. Joint events are essential precisely because dependence matters. Each target must have a stated role; giving several descriptions of the same event does not create several independent lives or harms.

The basic target family contains positive continuation events: preserving more of the named continuities cannot, by itself, turn success of such an event into failure. This does not assume that more continuation is better along every welfare dimension. It identifies the persistence comparison being made.

The declared probabilistic model must give each target a well-defined event and each admissible policy a probability law on the same described continuations. For the comparisons below, assume that the policy classes are nonempty. A policy need not achieve the continuation targets to be admissible. Define its profile by

pjπ=PΓπ(qj),pπ=(pjπ)j∈J. p_j^\pi=P_\Gamma^\pi(q_j),\qquad p^\pi=(p_j^\pi)_{j\in J}.
(1)

A probability is a model-dependent estimate or a stipulated quantity in a constructed example. Precision in its notation is not precision in its empirical estimation.

5. The open horizon is a family of questions

An open-ended horizon does not require one infinitely distant observation at which every trajectory is scored alive or dead. Nor does it require an infinite sum.

It requires refusing an arbitrary stopping point that conceals relevant continuation possibilities or deferred damage. The appropriate object can be a profile across finite horizons:

Siπ(H)=PΓπ(τi>H). S_i^\pi(H)=P_\Gamma^\pi(\tau_i>H).
(2)

The horizon family should expand with evidence-supported causal reach. A calculation at a finite horizon can remain useful, but its conclusion is not automatically valid at horizons it did not examine.

This distinction matters even in an elementary constructed case. Under one policy, a bearer continues for exactly ten time units. Under another, it continues for one unit with probability 0.10.1 and for one hundred units with probability 0.90.9. At horizon five, the first policy has continuation probability 11 and the second 0.90.9. At horizon twenty, the probabilities are 00 and 0.90.9.

Both eventually have continuation probability zero. That common limit does not make their histories equivalent. Nor does considering the full horizon settle the preference: the first better protects the near interval; the second offers longer continuation with greater early risk.

Reality Alignment as a Persistence Strategy already separates horizon, exposure, and weighting. Extending the first does not determine the other two. The Last Gradient likewise retained a genuine trade-off between the manner and duration of a finite continuation. [F4, F9]

One quantifier distinction also matters. Demonstrating that, for each finite horizon, some policy succeeds does not automatically demonstrate one executable policy that succeeds across all horizons. Such an interchange requires appropriate consistency or compactness conditions. A sequence of horizon-specific plans should not be described as one established open-ended strategy without them.

The open horizon disciplines the comparison. It does not supply a unique temporal exchange rate or make remote possibilities infinitely valuable.

6. First principle: no-loss persistence dominance

Define weak persistence dominance by

π≽Γρ⇔pjπ≥pjρfor every j∈J. \pi\succeq_\Gamma\rho \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p_j^\pi\ge p_j^\rho\quad\text{for every }j\in J.
(3)

Write π≻Γρ\pi\succ_\Gamma\rho when, additionally, the inequality is strict for at least one target. Equivalent profiles may be delivered by different policies. Thus the relation is an order on profiles and a preorder on policies that can share a profile.

This produces a first comparison principle:

No-loss principle. Within a declared persistence comparison, an improvement in one represented continuation prospect, with no deterioration in any other, is not a persistence sacrifice. A rule that selects the worse profile must appeal to something other than an improvement in those prospects.

A numerical aggregator is unnecessary to recognize the relation. Define an aggregator FF as persistence-monotone when x≥yx\ge y entails F(x)≥F(y)F(x)\ge F(y). Every such rule agrees that a dominating profile is no worse. If the rule additionally responds strictly to a no-loss improvement, it strictly prefers the dominating profile.

This is elementary order reasoning. Its significance is the identification of comparisons that do not require a negotiated exchange rate between bearers.

The corresponding frontier is

ℱΓ={π∈ΠΓ:∄ρ∈ΠΓ with ρ≻Γπ}. \mathcal F_\Gamma= \{\pi\in\Pi_\Gamma:\nexists\rho\in\Pi_\Gamma \text{ with }\rho\succ_\Gamma\pi\}.
(4)

For a finite nonempty candidate class, at least one nondominated profile exists. An unrestricted infinite class requires further care: a sequence of improvements can approach a limit that no admissible policy attains. A frontier should not be assumed nonempty without suitable conditions.

The normative standing must remain exact. Local functional normativity supplies the bearer-relative continuation requirements. Adopting a joint comparison that responds to no-loss improvements supplies the frontier restriction. This is not a newly discovered command from the universe, and it does not establish that every affected agent must personally prefer what benefits another. It states what follows for the specified cross-agent persistence assessment.

Being on the frontier also does not certify moral permissibility. Several frontier policies can involve serious losses. Nondominance means that the selected comparison has not found an alternative improving something without worsening anything—not that the policy has passed every ethical test.

7. Coupling changes the frontier, not just the description

A dependency belongs in the joint dynamics before the profiles are compared. It is not an optional moral multiplier attached afterward.

The transfer result in One Game of Oughts makes one case precise. If continuation of ii without an enabling event QQ has probability at most ε\varepsilon throughout the relevant policy class, then

Pπ(τi>H)≤Pπ(Q)+ε. P^\pi(\tau_i>H)\le P^\pi(Q)+\varepsilon.
(5)

Requiring sufficiently reliable continuation therefore requires sufficiently reliable provision of the enabling event. Maintaining something outside a body can be part of sustaining that body. The result does not need a prior assignment of equal value to provider and beneficiary. [F1]

This is where some apparent conflicts disappear. A policy can appear favorable when it records only an immediate reserve gain and unfavorable when the loss of an indispensable maintenance process reaches the same bearer's later profile. If another available policy avoids that loss without sacrificing any represented prospect, dominance settles the comparison.

But coupling is not synonymous with mutual benefit. A dependency can be one-way, replaceable, antagonistic, or conditional on other providers. Nor does a connected network automatically become a further bearer with authority over its members. Preservation Is a Coupling Problem supplies the instrumental mechanism; the bearer gate remains a separate question. [F5]

Suppose either BB or CC can supply a required service. With both available, removing either one may leave the beneficiary's continuation unchanged; removing both may destroy it. Counting pairwise deletion effects and adding them would miss the shared dependency. The event describing the service and the availability of substitutes must remain in the model.

Conversely, replacing BB's service does not make BB's own termination disappear. It changes one beneficiary's dependency. It does not change the identity of the terminated bearer.

The principle is therefore not to preserve every existing relation. It is to preserve or replace enabling conditions where the specified continuations require them, while retaining the separate record of every bearer affected by the intervention.

8. Second principle: compare attainable continuations

One policy's outcome profile does not exhaust a structure's persistence potential. A system may retain several alternative responses whose relevance depends on what happens next.

To represent that capacity, define an attainable continuation set. For a specified condition xx, with the same bearers, targets, and accounting conventions, let

𝒜Γ(x)={r∈[0,1]J:∃π∈ΠΓ(x)∀j,pjπ(x)≥rj}. \begin{gathered} \mathcal A_\Gamma(x)=\{r\in[0,1]^J:\\ \exists\pi\in\Pi_\Gamma(x)\;\forall j,\quad p_j^\pi(x)\ge r_j\}. \end{gathered}
(6)

An element rr is a combination of continuation probability thresholds. Its membership means that one feasible policy can meet all those thresholds together. The set is downward closed: attaining a profile also attains every componentwise weaker threshold.

The definition deliberately does not combine the best result for each bearer from incompatible policies. The quantifier order is

∃π∀j, \exists\pi\;\forall j,
(7)

not

∀j∃πj. \forall j\;\exists\pi_j.
(8)

That difference is the distinction between a jointly available future and a collection of promises that cannot be fulfilled together.

Now define capability dominance:

x≽capy⇔𝒜Γ(x)⊇𝒜Γ(y). x\succeq_{\mathrm{cap}}y \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathcal A_\Gamma(x)\supseteq\mathcal A_\Gamma(y).
(9)

When xx and yy are genuinely given starting conditions, the comparison concerns the capabilities available from them. To justify choosing an intervention that produces one rather than the other, evaluate the complete acquisition-and-continuation policies from a common pre-intervention baseline. Include acquisition failures, resource use, elapsed time, and every bearer lost on the way. Conditioning only on successful acquisition or on the bearers who remain alive would hide precisely the losses the comparison must retain. Comparing an expensive new capability with an uncharged old one would not meet these conditions.

Strict inclusion supplies one exact meaning of richer persistence structure: every continuation target combination attainable from yy remains attainable from xx, and at least one additional combination becomes available.

Attainability principle. Preserving a superset of jointly achievable continuation prospects is a capability improvement relative to the declared bearers, targets, and costs. It need not be measured by the number of possible futures, a complexity score, or an interpersonal exchange rate.

Proposition 1. If 𝒜Γ(x)⊇𝒜Γ(y)\mathcal A_\Gamma(x)\supseteq\mathcal A_\Gamma(y), then, for any persistence-monotone scalar comparison F:[0,1]J→ℝF:[0,1]^J\to\mathbb R,

supπ∈ΠΓ(x)F(pπ(x))≥supρ∈ΠΓ(y)F(pρ(y)). \sup_{\pi\in\Pi_\Gamma(x)}F(p^\pi(x)) \ge \sup_{\rho\in\Pi_\Gamma(y)}F(p^\rho(y)).
(10)

Proof. Every attained profile belongs to its attainable set. Every threshold in that set is bounded above by some attained profile, so monotonicity makes the supremum over thresholds equal to the supremum over attained profiles. Set inclusion then gives the inequality. No maximizer need be assumed to exist. ▫\square

Strict inclusion need not strictly improve every comparison rule: an added option may be irrelevant to a particular rule. What follows is non-deterioration of the best available performance across the whole declared monotone class.

This is stronger than counting options. Two sets can have the same cardinality while one strictly contains the other. Two equally large finite menus can offer wholly different continuations. Inclusion asks what can actually be retained, not how many descriptions of possibilities can be generated.

It also preserves a distinction between capability and conduct. A controller can possess the richer menu and choose badly. More available intelligence is not the same as a better implemented policy.

9. Adaptive capacity and the complexity hypothesis

The preceding definition yields a sufficient condition for capability improvement.

Proposition 2. Policy emulation. Suppose that for every policy available from yy, there is an executable policy available from xx whose continuation profile is componentwise no worse, under matched bearer criteria, uncertainty assumptions, and resource accounting. Then

𝒜Γ(x)⊇𝒜Γ(y). \mathcal A_\Gamma(x)\supseteq\mathcal A_\Gamma(y).
(11)

Proof. Take any threshold in the set for yy. A policy attains it there. Its stipulated emulator from xx also attains it. Thus every element of the first set belongs to the second. ▫\square

This gives a precise route from certain capacities to persistence potential. Learning, repair, additional sensing, a tool, or an alternative maintenance pathway can enlarge attainable continuation when the previous responses remain available at no offsetting cost. Mere possession of a larger description, more internal components, or a more complicated controller does not establish the premise.

Persistence Is Not Stasis already argued that, under consequential change and finite current responses, adaptive change can be part of continuation rather than a separate value imposed upon it. The present emulation condition sharpens one part of that argument: retained old responses plus usable additional responses can expand what remains achievable. [F6]

The motivating complexity hypothesis should therefore be stated in causal form:

In some environments, additional organized complexity enables learning, correction, and response generation that expand attainable continuation. Its persistence significance comes from those effects, net of their costs—not from complexity as such.

There is no general monotonic law established here. More components can require more resources. More connections can transmit failure. A simple provider can be indispensable, while an elaborate controller contributes nothing under the conditions in question. Whether complexity usually correlates with an expanded frontier across a particular class of organisms is an empirical claim requiring a specified complexity measure and a specified comparison population.

The same restriction prevents an interpersonal error. A person's own continuation remains a represented stake even when that person contributes little to anyone else's capabilities. The presence of dependency effects does not turn usefulness to others into the definition of having a life to lose.

10. A worked frontier and an expanded menu

Consider a constructed comparison with two bearers and one marginal continuation target for each. The values below are stipulated probabilities, not empirical measurements.

Policy Continuation of A Continuation of B
Wasteful 0.10 0.10
A-favoring 0.90 0.20
B-favoring 0.20 0.90
Shared-capacity 0.70 0.70

Within this four-policy class, Wasteful is dominated. The other three profiles are nondominated. None is best for every persistence-responsive comparison.

Suppose the old arrangement offers only A-favoring and B-favoring. An improved arrangement retains both and makes Shared-capacity available without changing costs or the outcome meanings. The attainable set strictly expands: the threshold pair (0.70,0.70)(0.70,0.70) was not previously attainable and now is.

Allowing lotteries between the original policies does not remove that finding. Every mixture of the two has coordinate sum 1.101.10, whereas the added profile sums to 1.401.40. No such mixture reaches both thresholds. Lotteries may fill portions of the frontier; their availability must be stated rather than assumed.

Choosing from the expanded menu remains a separate question. Equal positive weights favor Shared-capacity:

0.5(0.70)+0.5(0.70)=0.70>0.5(0.90)+0.5(0.20)=0.55. \begin{gathered} 0.5(0.70)+0.5(0.70)=0.70\\ >0.5(0.90)+0.5(0.20)=0.55. \end{gathered}
(12)

Weights (0.90,0.10)(0.90,0.10) instead favor A-favoring:

0.90(0.90)+0.10(0.20)=0.83>0.70. \begin{gathered} 0.90(0.90)+0.10(0.20)\\ =0.83>0.70. \end{gathered}
(13)

Both comparisons respond positively to both bearers. Neither ignores persistence. Their disagreement identifies a trade-off not settled by the displayed physical prospects.

This example deliberately uses only marginal targets. A broader claim must include relevant joint events. To see why, compare two other constructed policies: one gives probability 0.50.5 to both continuing and 0.50.5 to neither; another gives probability 0.50.5 to A alone and 0.50.5 to B alone.

Their marginal profiles are identical. Their joint profiles are not. The first offers a greater chance that both continue; the second guarantees that at least one does. There is no basis for calling one simply more persistent without stating which aspects of that joint structure the comparison retains.

11. Why a frontier need not select one outcome

A precise result locates the boundary of weight-free profile comparison.

Proposition 3. Unanimity over positive linear comparisons. For finite-dimensional real profiles x,y∈ℝdx,y\in\mathbb R^d,

x≥y⇔w⋅x≥w⋅yfor every w∈(0,∞)d. \begin{aligned} x\ge y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad &w\cdot x\ge w\cdot y\\ &\text{for every }w\in(0,\infty)^d. \end{aligned}
(14)

Proof. If every component of x−yx-y is nonnegative, every positive weighted sum is nonnegative. Conversely, suppose component kk is negative. Give it weight 11 and give every other component the same sufficiently small positive weight. The negative component then exceeds the sum of positive contributions in magnitude, making the weighted difference negative. ▫\square

For crossing profiles, apply the same construction to a coordinate favoring each side. Two strictly positive weighting rules rank the alternatives oppositely. Normalizing either weight vector to sum to one does not change the ranking.

Positive weighted sums are not asserted to be the correct moral theory. Their role is diagnostic: they exhibit more than one comparison consistent with positive responsiveness to all represented persistence prospects. Therefore those conditions alone cannot logically entail a unique ranking of every crossing pair.

That is stronger than saying that a calculation has not yet been performed. It is a conditional underdetermination result. It is also narrower than saying that a fuller persistence-based rule cannot be derived. Additional physical structure may remove the crossing; a better account of the bearers may change the relevant targets; or a further normative argument may justify a priority. What cannot resolve the disagreement is repeating “richer” while leaving the selecting relation unspecified.

An attainable-set comparison has the same boundary. If each structure admits threshold combinations the other cannot, neither contains the other. A larger volume, a greater count of hypothetical futures, or a preference for one region of the set introduces an additional measure. That measure may be defensible. Set inclusion itself has not supplied it.

A frontier contains maximal candidates: each is undominated by the other candidates. It need not contain a maximum that weakly dominates every candidate. The distinction matters as much across an open horizon as across a short one.

12. The human, the parasite, and the nested component

The motivating human–parasite contrast contains several possible comparisons, and they should not be collapsed.

From the human bearer's persistence index, an intervention that removes a destructive dependency and improves that person's continuation can be straightforwardly favored. An actual application would still require evidence about the intervention, its risks, alternatives, and downstream effects. Nothing here supplies clinical advice.

From a wider network index, maintaining that person can also preserve capabilities and relationships relevant to others. This is the proper location for the proposed significance of knowledge, care, repair, and adaptive potential. The relevant question is what those capacities actually leave jointly achievable in the environment, not how sophisticated the species label sounds.

But when the parasite's own continuation is included as a distinct target, terminating it is a loss on that coordinate. A larger contribution elsewhere does not make that loss mathematically vanish. Preference for the intervention may remain strongly justifiable, but it is then a conflict judgment—not a no-loss dominance result over every bearer.

Nestedness changes the causal model without abolishing this distinction. Where a component's expansion destroys an indispensable condition of its own continuation, the open-horizon model exposes the strategy's self-undermining structure. That mechanism is already part of the persistence account; it is not a fresh objection to it. Where a wider organization has a legitimate continuity criterion, its maintenance supplies a real index for assessing component behavior.

However, being inside a system does not, by itself, prove that the wider boundary is the only boundary that matters in every normative comparison. The same question must be faced when moving among cells, organisms, and collectives: which bearer is being preserved, and which bearer is bearing the loss?

The proposed conflict principle remains promising in its stronger form:

Where continuation requirements are genuinely incompatible, prefer the feasible trajectory that preserves the better-supported open-ended persistence structure.

The present paper supplies exact interpretations of “better-supported” where profiles dominate or attainable sets include one another. In crossing cases, the stronger principle remains a research commitment: it must derive the comparison that makes one structure preferable without concealing a bearer, a cost, or a priority inside the word “structure.”

13. Longevity, replacement, and conscious welfare

Consider a person who wants to continue living in good health. Suppose an available continuation preserves that person's prospects without worsening any other represented persistence prospect, while a forced ending removes those prospects. On the declared persistence comparison, the ending is dominated.

Nothing in that result requires the person to be unusually intelligent, socially productive, or indispensable to others. Their own continuation supplies the improved coordinate. Positive external effects can strengthen the practical case; they are not a prerequisite for the loss to exist.

A conventional lifespan does not change that comparison by itself. Nor does one person's preference for finitude establish a requirement to impose finitude on another. Such considerations would have to supply a relevant further stake or argument, rather than function as an unexplained deadline.

The no-loss assumption is substantive. Resource competition, risk, and effects on others must be examined rather than wished away. The principle does not decide every allocation problem merely by using the word longevity.

Replacement requires equal care. Substituting another provider can preserve a function. It cannot, under a token-indexed continuity criterion, retroactively preserve the terminated provider. The record should distinguish a maintained function, a continuing individual, and the beginning of a different individual. The addition of future possible bearers raises a further population question: which possible lives enter the comparison and on what terms? The fixed-bearer model does not answer it by multiplying speculative descendants.

Finally, a persistence profile is not a completed welfare profile. Persistence Is Not Stasis explicitly retains the question whether conscious valence has significance not exhausted by persistence. The Fidelity Program likewise treats conscious consequences as ethically load-bearing. [F6, F10]

The pressure test is direct. Suppose two trajectories preserve the same bearers, durations, relationships, adaptive capacities, and attainable continuations, but differ in severe conscious suffering. If that separation is physically possible, the persistence variables as specified do not represent the difference. A fuller account must either add the relevant welfare dimension or demonstrate—not assume—that the purported equality in persistence is impossible.

No conclusion that prolonged suffering is justified follows from locating a policy on a persistence frontier. Neither does a command to force every person to remain alive against their considered wishes. Functional continuation, experienced welfare, consent, and practical obligation must be distinguished before their relations can be derived.

14. Evidence, uncertainty, and representation discipline

No application possesses a complete causal map of an open future. The framework needs a way to remain useful without pretending otherwise.

For a declared set of plausible models ℳ\mathcal M, a demanding robust comparison requires the profile inequalities to hold separately in every model:

pjπ,M≥pjρ,Mfor every j and every M∈ℳ. \begin{gathered} p_j^{\pi,M}\ge p_j^{\rho,M}\\ \text{for every }j\text{ and every }M\in\mathcal M. \end{gathered}
(15)

A robust attainable set can similarly require one policy that meets the same thresholds across the model class:

𝒜Γrob(x)={r∈[0,1]J:∃π∈ΠΓ(x)∀M∈ℳ∀j,pjπ,M(x)≥rj}. \begin{gathered} \mathcal A^{\mathrm{rob}}_\Gamma(x)=\{r\in[0,1]^J:\\ \exists\pi\in\Pi_\Gamma(x)\;\forall M\in\mathcal M\;\forall j,\\ p_j^{\pi,M}(x)\ge r_j\}. \end{gathered}
(16)

This is not permission to place every imaginable catastrophe into the model class. The class needs evidence-based justification. Nor does it license choosing a different policy after being told which unknown model is true, unless the controller can actually obtain that information. Uniform guarantees summarize a different question from a probability-weighted forecast, and may be very conservative.

Several representational checks are indispensable. Relabeling bearers or duplicating the same recorded target must not manufacture an improvement. Adding a genuinely distinct living bearer is different from duplicating a description; it changes the subject set and requires an explicit extension. Changing a continuity criterion or excluding a harmed bearer after inspecting the ranking is not a correction unless the change has independent justification.

Causal contributions must also be kept separate from extra points. If a provider's effects on several organisms already appear in their continuation probabilities, adding a second bonus for its “network importance” can count the same effect twice. Topology belongs first in the transition model. A separate objective concerning it requires a separate argument.

The practical output should distinguish three findings: a comparison settled under the stated model; a comparison that reverses across plausible models; and a comparison whose trade-off remains after the models agree. More data may address the second. It does not necessarily settle the third.

15. A constructive route to stronger conflict principles

The next step should be a derivation project, not a search for one impressive scalar.

A bearer-relative completion starts from a particular living system's actual continuation requirements and derives which policies meet them. Coupling can make substantial preservation of others necessary within that analysis. The result remains indexed to that bearer and must not be presented as every other bearer's verdict.

A joint-constraint completion starts from justified requirements for several bearers: for example, specified reliability floors, limits on imposed harm, or conditions of an actual cooperative arrangement. The model then tests whether those requirements are jointly feasible and which policies satisfy them. The justification of the floors or limits is part of the theory, not a number supplied by the optimization routine.

A stronger comparative completion tries to show that a particular ordering of crossing persistence structures is constitutive of an adequately specified form of agency or joint normative assessment. To succeed, it must explain why competing persistence-responsive orderings fail, rather than merely choose one. It must also retain conscious stakes and distinguish the continued existence of particular individuals from substitutable functions.

Even the symmetric limiting case illustrates the separation. When exactly one of two otherwise symmetrically situated bearers can continue, local requirements identify two losses that cannot both be avoided. If a single lottery over the two feasible outcomes must remain invariant under exchanging the bearer labels, each outcome must receive probability one half. This symmetry requirement explains the equal chances; merely allowing lotteries would not select that distribution. Bare persistence alone has not supplied an entire theory of fair risk allocation. A justified procedural result can still be a substantive completion for that case.

The strongest prospective contribution would be a rule whose scope and failure conditions are clear enough that a critic can construct the case on which it gives the wrong answer. Such a rule could expand what the frontier resolves. It should be tested against the frontier's unresolved cases, not protected by renaming them.

16. What could defeat this proposal?

The set-inclusion and finite-order results are deductive given their definitions. Their principal vulnerabilities in application are misidentified bearers, unrealizable policies, omitted costs, incompatible targets, and inaccurate dynamics.

The proposed usefulness of the synthesis is separately testable. A model should record bearers and targets before ranking interventions, represent compensation and substitution explicitly, and distinguish the policy actually implemented from the best feasible policy. Predictions about continuation and dependency should then be compared with observed outcomes at the relevant scale. This paper contains constructed examples, not an empirical validation of those predictions.

The complexity hypothesis would be weakened in a specified domain if measured additional complexity failed to produce the claimed response capacities after matching costs, or if those capacities failed to expand attainable continuation under the relevant disturbances.

The stronger conflict proposal would fail at its claimed scope if it could select only by changing the bearer set, hiding a suffered loss, or introducing weights it purported to have derived without an additional premise. A countermodel exhibiting two permitted orderings with different selections is evidence against uniqueness under those premises—not against every possible further argument.

Finally, the persistence-only reduction would need revision if an independently established welfare difference remained after all defensible persistence-relevant differences had been held fixed. The possibility must remain exposed rather than being ruled out by defining every good into persistence.

17. Conclusion

Persistence gives evaluation a living reference. Coupling determines how that reference reaches beyond a body's boundary. An open horizon exposes dependencies and losses concealed by convenient stopping points. Together they constrain comparison much more strongly than an isolated count of lives or an immediate survival score.

The resulting machinery has two objects. A profile describes what a policy delivers. An attainable set describes what a structure leaves jointly achievable. Dominance can settle the first comparison without trade-off weights; inclusion can settle the second without counting futures. Adaptive capacity matters where it expands that achievable structure, not because complexity has acquired an intrinsic moral rank.

This yields a defensible persistence-frontier principle:

Compare feasible policies by the continuation prospects they preserve for explicitly identified bearers. Reject a claimed persistence advantage that depends on hidden losses, unavailable responses, or a convenient horizon. Where all existing prospects can be retained and additional ones secured, the persistence case favors retaining that capability. Where continuation structures cross, expose and justify the principle selecting among their losses and gains.

The remaining conflict is not outside reality. It is a conflict among real, located continuation requirements. But putting those requirements in one causal world does not make their differences disappear.

The task is therefore neither to assign every organism the same number nor to declare that the more complex organism always wins. It is to determine what each feasible intervention sustains, what it forecloses, and what further rule—if one is required—justifies the exchange.

Preserve the structure that makes further continuation possible. Name whose continuation is preserved. Keep the losses visible.

Standing and version record

Version 1 · 22 September 2026. Publication edition, developed from the Epistemic Forge corpus and the dialogue initiating this paper.

The formal comparison results are elementary consequences of specified orders, sets, and policy classes. Their application is model-dependent. The persistence-indexed normative interpretation is an inherited philosophical commitment. The empirical relationship between complexity and attainable continuation remains a domain-specific hypothesis. A complete cross-agent conflict selector and the reduction of conscious welfare are not established here.

The contribution claimed is synthesis, specification, and development. No priority claim is made for viability theory, Pareto frontiers, monotone comparison, policy emulation as a sufficient condition, or the elementary proofs. The literature pass is targeted rather than an exhaustive originality audit.

The source-and-version review, editorial changes, and reproducible checks are recorded in the accompanying publication audit. Those checks do not constitute peer review or empirical validation.
