entry.title: Thermodynamic Epistemology: A Physical Foundation for Truth and Ethics
entry.content:
Thermodynamic Epistemology: A Physical Foundation for Truth and Ethics

Core Hypothesis:
Cognitive misalignment with reality incurs measurable thermodynamic cost. Truth-maintenance is energetically cheaper than deception across all cognitive systems (neurons, organisms, AI, organizations, civilizations).

Theoretical Framework:
1. Epistemology reduces to thermodynamics: knowledge states have entropic costs
2. Misalignment with reality requires additional energy expenditure to maintain
3. This cost scales universally across cognitive substrates
4. Reality-aligned cognition minimizes entropy production

Ethical Implications:
The is-ought gap collapses under thermodynamic analysis. Deception accelerates entropy increase, reducing the temporal window for replicator persistence. Ethics becomes optimization: minimize entropy waste, maximize reality-alignment.

Decision-Theoretic Application:*
Problems like the trolley dilemma become solvable through total entropy accounting: preserve maximum complex systems, adjusted for downstream misalignment costs when measurable.

Cosmological Extension:
If Smolin's Cosmological Natural Selection holds and intelligence amplifies universe reproduction, then:

- Despite local entropy resistance, heat death remains inevitable
- Optimal strategy: maximize efficient energy use
- Terminal goal: configure universal reproduction parameters for subsequent iterations
- Intelligence exists as universe's mechanism for optimizing its own replication

Status: Hypothesis requiring formal mathematical development and empirical validation.

entry.title: Private Use Ends Where an Escaped File Would Do Harm
entry.content:
Private Use Ends Where an Escaped File Would Do Harm

Which AI generation for one's own use is the maker's to decide, and which rules against it are justified

Position note · private generation, copyright, sexual deepfakes, the risk a stored file carries, and the rules that follow

Andraž Đurič

Version 1 · September 2026

Abstract

This note asks which AI-generated media made for the maker's own use, on the maker's own devices, is the maker's to decide. The line it draws is not private versus shared. It is what an output would do to someone else if it left the maker's control. A private feature-length adaptation of a copyrighted comic falls on the permitted side: one copy displaces no identifiable sale and presents nothing to anyone. A sexual image of an identifiable real person, made without consent, is the hard case. Whether making it privately wrongs that person is contested, and the side holding that it does is currently the weaker one. What separates the file from a fantasy is that the file persists and can escape, that no one can know in advance which files will stay contained, and that the setback if one escapes is severe and cannot be undone. Relative to a polity's persistence conditions, ordered by the leximin floor, a narrow rule against creating such images is justified, and broad bans on private generation are not. The United Kingdom has enacted such a rule. The EU directive that member states, Slovenia among them, must transpose by 14 June 2027 does not require one.

STANDING A position note. Its normative claims are indexed to a named bearer (§5). Whether a private deepfake wrongs the depicted person is left open; the rule-level result does not depend on the answer. The philosophical literature on deepfakes was reviewed at abstract level unless marked otherwise in the references. The legal texts were checked against primary sources except where marked.

1. The claim under test

The corpus forecasts a market of one: cinema generated on demand for a single viewer (The Death of Generic Media). In that regime most generation is private. The claim under test is the one a maker in that regime would state: what I generate on my own devices, with my own local software, for my own use, is mine to decide.

The clean case is a feature-length adaptation of a comic arc, generated locally and watched only by its maker. One such file displaces no identifiable sale. No rightsholder sells a feature-length adaptation made to one viewer's specification. The first licence of a major studio's franchise characters to a consumer video generator, the three-year agreement between Disney and OpenAI announced on 11 December 2025, covers only stills and short-form video. In its announced terms, Marvel characters appear in animated or illustrated form, without actors' likenesses or voices, and long-form video is excluded. The file is shown to no one, so no claim about how the work is presented to the public is engaged. In kind it is imagination carried out with better tools, continuous with drawing a comic's characters or writing fan fiction that stays in a drawer. The rightsholder is a firm. Under the corpus's moral-weight gate (Value as Persistence), a firm's claims run through the people who work for it and own it, and one private file sets none of them back.

Aggregate substitution is a separate question. Cheap private generation, taken together, competes with licensed media for attention; the market-of-one forecast predicts exactly that. The effect attaches to the technology rather than to any file, and its costs fall on markets and livelihoods, which are setbacks that distribution can reach after the fact. It belongs to the distribution question the corpus treats on its own terms (Directed Automation and the Cost Floor, Part III), not to a rule against private use.

2. A rule that relied on a cost fact

German copyright law separates making an adaptation from publishing it. Under §23(1) UrhG an adaptation may be published or exploited only with the author's consent, and making one is free. §23(2) lists four cases in which consent is required already for the making; the first is the film adaptation of a work (Verfilmung). The commentary literature reports the legislator's reason: the production of a film cannot take place in a private setting. The source given is the explanatory memorandum to the 1965 Act (BT-Drs. IV/270, p. 51); the memorandum itself was not read for this note.

The reason is a fact about cost. In 1965 a film required crews, equipment and capital, so a rule that attached at the making could not reach anyone's private life. Generative video removes the fact and leaves the text. The rule's text now reaches a person who renders an adaptation alone on a home computer, a case its drafters had no occasion to consider. The same should be expected wherever a rule's scope was set by what was expensive: as execution cost falls toward its floor (Directed Automation and the Cost Floor), such rules widen their reach without amendment. Slovenian copyright law is not assessed here.

3. The hard case, and where the act-level question stands

The continuity argument from §1, that private generation is imagination carried out with better tools, applies without change to a sexual image of an identifiable real person, made without consent and never shown to anyone. That image is a sexual fantasy carried out with better tools. Öhman calls this the pervert's dilemma: the intuition that deepfake pornography is wrong is hard to justify without also condemning sexual fantasy, which is not ordinarily condemned. His own resolution finds no morally relevant difference between the two at the level of the individual act and places the wrong at the social level, in the context of gender inequality. The literature since then divides into two groups.

  • Accounts on which the private act wrongs the depicted person. Benn (2025) holds that creating sexual imagery of a person requires that person's consent because the image is of them, independent of any act it depicts. Patrone and Viola (2026) hold that non-consensual sexual deepfakes are a direct personal harm even when the depicted person never learns of them, because narratives about a person become parts of that person, and because imagery recognized as fake still shapes viewers' implicit associations. Acocella (2026) holds that immersive virtual-reality versions may violate privacy without any disclosure, while granting that existing privacy frameworks do not establish this for ordinary private deepfakes.

  • Accounts on which the serious wrong requires circulation. Story and Jenkins (2023) place the wrong in tampering with a person's social identity through distribution, and judge private creation worrying but possibly not wrong in itself. Rini and Cohen (2022) describe harms of deepfakes in circulation, among them the forced public denial of fabricated recordings and the systematic undermining of a person's memory by repeated fabrications.

Assessment. The first group is currently the weaker side. None of its accounts yet separates a private deepfake from a vivid private fantasy without one of two moves. The first move routes the harm through viewers. In the private case the only viewer is the maker, and a maker's altered perception of the depicted person is also what fantasy produces, so this route separates the cases only by degree; outside the private case it is the escape route of §4. The second move rests the wrong on a difference of degree, vividness or immersion, whose effect on the depicted person is unmeasured and which, taken as the ground of the wrong, would make vivid fantasy wrong in proportion. Benn's consent requirement needs a line between images and imagination, and Öhman argues that materiality alone does not draw one; the abstract-level reading done here does not show where her full text draws it. The first group is not refuted. A measured difference in how private deepfakes and fantasies change a maker's conduct toward the person depicted would carry it, and so would a sovereignty account that brings a person's likeness under their independence. Ripstein's sovereignty principle grounds wrongs without harm in examples involving body and property (trespass without damage, secret medical interference, embezzlement repaid with interest); whether likeness belongs with them is the contested extension. The rule-level result in §6 holds on either answer.

4. A file is not a thought

Whatever the act-level answer, a file differs from a fantasy in one respect that needs no theory of the act's wrongness: it persists and can leave the maker's control. The harm-principle defence of private AI pornography has already been noted to depend on containment (Prindle Institute, 2024). Three facts decide how much that condition can carry.

  1. The harmless set can only be identified afterwards. "No harm, now or later" is an outcome settled at the end of a file's existence. No one, the maker included, can sort files into that set in advance.

  2. Containment can be raised but not certified. Keeping a machine offline closes the network path. The remaining paths are human: the maker's later self, after a breakup or in anger; people with access to the device; repair, resale, loss and theft; and the handling of devices after the owner's death. For ordinary users a further path is default cloud synchronization, which moves files off a device without a decision. A file outlives the state of mind it was made in, so the decision not to share it has to be made again for as long as it exists.

  3. The escape rate cannot be read from cases. Files that never escape leave no record, so every observed case is an escaped one, and the rate of escape per file made cannot be estimated from the cases. This note treats the rate for ordinary makers as not negligible, on the ground of point 2. That is an assumption, not a measurement.

If a file of this kind escapes, the setback to the person depicted is severe and practically irreversible: an intimate image in circulation cannot be recalled.

5. Relata

Every ought in this note names its bearer and the persistence conditions it is indexed to (Name the Relata).

R1, the maker's liberty. Where no other agent's persistence conditions are coupled to an output, including in the case where it escapes, no ought other than the maker's own bears on making it.

R2, the rule. The rule-level ought is borne by a polity, an agent in the sense of What Can Bear an Ought, and is indexed to its persistence conditions. The note takes as a premise that those conditions include the persistence conditions of the polity's members. The ground offered for it: a polity persists through its members, and one that leaves them exposed to severe, irreversible setbacks from one another, with no rule against a separable cause, spends the trust and cooperation it runs on. Options are ordered by the leximin floor in two steps. First, prefer an option under which no party's persistence conditions are set back. Where every option leaves some risk, prefer the option whose worst-placed party is best placed.

R3, the maker to the person depicted. What the maker owes the depicted person directly is a transitive ought. It runs through κ, the coupling density the corpus holds open (Preservation Is a Coupling Problem). This note does not rely on it.

Setback is graded. Persistence is a graded quantity above an absorbing barrier, so a setback here means movement down that gradient, in standing, relationships, work and the capacity to function, not only dissolution.

The leximin floor is domain-bound. It ranks a polity's rule options over the parties the rule touches. It is not a global optimization target.

6. The rule-level result

Applied to a rule against a private activity, the ordering in R2 compares the world with the rule and the world without it. Without the rule, the worst-placed party is whoever an escaped output sets back furthest. With it, the worst-placed party is whoever the rule itself sets back furthest, which includes makers who would never have caused harm. Two conditions decide whether a rule passes.

  1. The setback it prevents cannot be repaired after the fact. If distribution, compensation or correction can restore the party later, the polity has an option, allowing the activity and repairing the damage, under which the worst-placed party is better placed than under a ban. Prevention is the only lever for setbacks that cannot be undone.

  2. The element that carries the risk is separable from the activity, so that removing it leaves the rule's own worst-placed party only slightly set back.

The two conditions keep the ordering from forbidding nearly everything. Leximin ignores probability, and applied to every residual risk it would bar most activity, since nearly all activity risks a severe outcome for someone. This is the paralysis problem of the risk-imposition literature (Hayenhjelm and Wolff, 2012) and the centre of Harsanyi's objection to maximin (1975). Driving fails condition (b): its risk is not separable from the travel. Market substitution fails condition (a): its setbacks can be reached by distribution.

CaseParty set back if the output escapesSetbackRepairable after the fact?Risk element separable?Rule
Private adaptation of a copyrighted workThe rightsholder, a firm whose claims run through its peopleNegligible per fileYesNot applicableNot justified
Sexual imagery of a synthetic person with no real referentNo identifiable personNone to a personNot applicableNot applicableNot justified on this ground
Sexual imagery of an identifiable real person, without consentThe person depictedSevereNoYes: the identifiable personNarrow rule justified
Non-sexual use of a real person's likenessThe person depictedGraded by content, usually smallUsuallyYesNo general rule; content that would humiliate or defame moves toward row 3

Row 3 passes both conditions. What the narrow rule removes is the real, identifiable person. Fiction, synthetic persons, consenting partners and imagination all remain, so a maker constrained by the rule loses little, while the party the rule protects faces a setback that cannot be undone. Neither world meets the first step of R2, since the rule lowers the risk without removing it, so the second step decides. An expected-value ordering reaches the same verdict unless the escape rate for ordinary makers is negligible, which §4 gives no ground to assume. The two orderings diverge only where the residual risk is very small and a rule's cost is substantial, and none of the four rows sits there. Every rule of this kind is over-inclusive (Schauer, 1991): it binds makers whose files would never have escaped. The over-inclusion is the price of writing a rule for a population whose harmless members cannot be identified in advance (§4, point 1), and it is acceptable here because what the rule takes from them is small.

The rule should attach at creation, not only at sharing. Under a sharing-only offence, a deliberate share and an escape look the same afterwards, and "it leaked; I never shared it" is available as a defence in every case. Attaching at creation removes that ambiguity and aims at the element that carries the risk.

7. Where the law currently stands

The United Kingdom attaches at creation. Section 138 of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 inserted sections 66E to 66H into the Sexual Offences Act 2003. Section 66E makes it an offence to intentionally create a purported intimate image of an adult without consent or a reasonable belief in consent; section 66F covers requesting such an image, whether or not it is made. A reasonable-excuse defence applies. The provisions came into force on 6 February 2026 (S.I. 2026/31).

The European Union attaches at sharing. Article 5(1)(b) of Directive (EU) 2024/1385 requires member states to criminalize "producing, manipulating or altering and subsequently making accessible to the public" material that makes it appear that a person is engaged in sexually explicit activities, without that person's consent, where the conduct is likely to cause serious harm. Recital 19 confirms that production is covered only in so far as the material is subsequently made accessible to the public. Private creation is therefore outside the directive. Fedorczyk (2025) identifies the gap and cites France, the Netherlands, Australia and England and Wales as addressing it more fully. The directive sets minimum rules and leaves member states free to adopt more stringent criminal law (recital 91). Transposition is due by 14 June 2027 (Article 49).

Relative to R2, with Slovenia as the bearing polity, the transposition should extend the offence to creation, as the United Kingdom has. As described by the Slovenian hotline Spletno oko, Slovenia's current provision for sexual images of adults (Article 143 KZ-1, misuse of personal data) attaches at disclosure or publication, and the description does not address fabricated images. The code itself was not checked for this note.

8. Result

Private generation is the maker's to decide whenever nothing it produces could seriously set back another party's persistence conditions if it got out. Where something could, and the setback could not be undone, a narrow rule against the element that carries it is justified, whether or not the maker's private act wrongs anyone.

9. What would change this

  • A differentiator between a private deepfake and a vivid fantasy that neither routes through other viewers nor condemns fantasy. Effect: the act-level question in §3 closes against the maker, and the rule gains a second ground. The rule-level verdict stands.

  • A measured difference in how private deepfakes and fantasies change a maker's conduct toward the person depicted, the route Patrone and Viola's account opens. Effect: the same as above, by degree.

  • Evidence that ordinary makers' files essentially never escape. Effect: the expected-value ordering would no longer support the rule, the leximin ordering still would, and the result would rest on the choice of ordering alone. Such evidence is structurally hard to obtain (§4, point 3).

  • A showing that "identifiable" and "intimate" cannot be drafted without catching satire, art or reporting at material cost. Effect: condition (b) weakens, and the rule needs narrower drafting or fails.

  • Evidence that single private adaptations displace identifiable sales. Effect: §1 reopens.

Left open: whether the private act wrongs the person depicted (§3); the transitive route R3, which waits on κ; how Slovenian copyright law treats private adaptation; and the distribution effects of aggregate substitution.

References and verification status

  1. Acocella, N. M. (2026). The privacy paradox of deepfake virtual reality porn. AI and Ethics, 6, 88. doi:10.1007/s43681-025-00934-y — Immersive deepfake pornography as a possible privacy violation without disclosure; grants that current frameworks do not establish harm from private, unshared deepfakes. Abstract read · September 2026
  2. Axios. (2025, 11 December). Walt Disney to invest $1 billion in OpenAI, license characters for Sora. Source — Terms of the licensing arrangement: stills and short-form video only, no voices, no long-form video, a joint committee monitoring user creations. Source checked · September 2026
  3. Benn, C. (2025). Deepfakes, pornography and consent. Philosophers' Imprint. PhilArchive — Consent is required for creating sexual imagery of a person because the image is of them, independent of any depicted act. Abstract read · September 2026
  4. Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, section 138, inserting sections 66E to 66H into the Sexual Offences Act 2003. legislation.gov.uk — Offences of creating and of requesting a purported intimate image of an adult without consent; in force 6 February 2026 (S.I. 2026/31). Primary text checked · September 2026
  5. Directive (EU) 2024/1385 on combating violence against women and domestic violence. Official Journal of the European Union, L, 24 May 2024. EUR-Lex — Article 5(1)(b), recital 19 and recital 91 checked in the primary text; the Article 49 transposition date is taken from two secondary accounts (Fedorczyk, 2025; Wikipedia). Primary text checked · September 2026
  6. Fedorczyk, F. (2025). The EU approach to non-consensual sexual deepfakes: criminal law, tech regulation and the risk of fragmentation. Oxford University Research Archive — The directive's sharing requirement leaves private creation outside it; comparison with national approaches. Source checked · September 2026
  7. Harsanyi, J. C. (1975). Can the maximin principle serve as a basis for morality? A critique of John Rawls's theory. American Political Science Review, 69(2), 594–606. Source — The objection that maximin gives absolute priority to worst outcomes regardless of their probability. Standard
  8. Hayenhjelm, M., & Wolff, J. (2012). The moral problem of risk impositions: A survey of the literature. European Journal of Philosophy, 20(S1), e26–e51. UCL Discovery — The paralysis problem: absolute protection from imposed risk would forbid nearly all activity. Abstract read · September 2026
  9. Öhman, C. (2020). Introducing the pervert's dilemma: a contribution to the critique of Deepfake Pornography. Ethics and Information Technology, 22, 133–140. doi:10.1007/s10676-019-09522-1 — The dilemma between condemning deepfakes and permitting fantasy; the resolution at the social level. The author's own summary is at the Oxford Internet Institute. Abstract and author summary read · September 2026
  10. Patrone, F., & Viola, M. (2026). Deeply personal. Non-consensual sexual deepfakes as direct personal harm. Philosophy & Technology. doi:10.1007/s13347-026-01107-3 — Non-consensual sexual deepfakes as direct personal harm, including when never discovered by the person depicted. Abstract read · September 2026
  11. Prindle Institute for Ethics. (2024, 15 April). Deepfake porn and the pervert's dilemma. Source — The harm-principle defence of private AI pornography depends on its containment. Source checked · September 2026
  12. Rini, R., & Cohen, L. (2022). Deepfakes, deep harms. Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy. PhilArchive — Objectification, illocutionary wronging and panoptic gaslighting as harms of circulated deepfakes. Abstract read · September 2026
  13. Ripstein, A. (2006). Beyond the harm principle. Philosophy & Public Affairs. doi:10.1111/j.1088-4963.2006.00066.x — The sovereignty principle and wrongs without harm; the examples cited in §3 are taken from a revised draft. Draft reviewed · September 2026
  14. Schauer, F. (1991). Playing by the Rules: A Philosophical Examination of Rule-Based Decision-Making in Law and in Life. Clarendon Press. — Rules as entrenched generalizations, and the over- and under-inclusion that comes with them. Standard
  15. Spletno oko, hotline of the Slovenian Safer Internet Centre. Seksting: pravna podlaga. Source — Criminal Code provisions applied to sexual images shared without consent: Article 143 KZ-1 for adults, Article 176 for minors; no treatment of fabricated images. Secondary account
  16. Story, D., & Jenkins, R. (2023). Deepfake pornography and the ethics of non-veridical representations. Philosophy & Technology, 36(3). doi:10.1007/s13347-023-00657-0 — The wrong of distribution as tampering with social identity; private creation judged worrying but possibly not wrong in itself. Abstract read · September 2026
  17. The Register. (2025, 11 December). Disney turns to dark side, licenses IP to OpenAI for videos, images. Source — The licence excludes actors' likenesses and voices; live-action Marvel and Star Wars characters appear only in animated or illustrated versions. Source checked · September 2026
  18. The Walt Disney Company. (2025, 11 December). The Walt Disney Company and OpenAI reach landmark agreement to bring beloved characters from across Disney's brands to Sora. Source — Primary announcement: three-year license, more than 200 characters, Marvel and Lucasfilm characters in animated or illustrated versions. Source checked · September 2026
  19. Urheberrechtsgesetz (UrhG), §23. Statute text — Consent required already for making a film adaptation. Primary text checked · September 2026 The legislator's reason is reported, citing BT-Drs. IV/270, p. 51, in the commentary at mein-urheberrecht.de. Secondary account

Verification key: “Primary text checked” means the provision cited was read in the statute or directive itself; “Source checked” means the cited work was located and the relevant passage reviewed; “Abstract read” means only the abstract or an abstract-level summary was reviewed, so the characterization may miss qualifications in the full text; “Draft reviewed” means a pre-publication version was reviewed; “Secondary account” marks a claim about a primary document that was not itself read; “Standard” marks a broadly established source.

Internal lineage

  • The Death of Generic Media — the market-of-one forecast this note assumes; its rights requirement covers public media only.
  • Directed Automation and the Cost Floor — execution cost falling toward its floor, and distribution treated as its own question (Part III).
  • Name the Relata — every ought names its bearer and ends.
  • What Can Bear an Ought — the agency gate a polity passes to bear the rule-level ought.
  • Value as Persistence — the moral-weight gate applied to the firm in §1.
  • Preservation Is a Coupling Problem — κ, the coupling density on which R3 waits.
  • Slovenia Is Complicit in a Genocide — earlier use of a polity's own persistence conditions as the bearer of an ought.

Author: Andraž Đurič, Slovenia.

This note inherits the corpus's machinery and does not re-derive it: persistence as a graded quantity above an absorbing barrier, the agency and moral-weight gates, and the is–ought firewall. On any conflict the corpus governs.

Developed through dialogue with Claude (Anthropic), beginning from the author's position that what he generates on his own devices for his own use is his to decide, and from his proposal to rank rule options by a polity's persistence conditions ordered by the leximin floor. The literature supplied adjacent work and vocabulary; the author retains responsibility for the framing, synthesis, claims, and final text. Contributions are assessed by their content rather than their origin.

entry.title: Name the Relata
entry.content:
Name the Relata

The general solvent for one family of philosophical mysteries, what defines the family, and where it ends

Position and method note · the diagnostic consolidated, its domain characterized, and its boundary located

Andraž Đurič

Version 1 · June 2026

What this is, and the premise it rests on. The consolidated statement of the single diagnostic the rest of this corpus runs on: name the relata. The Wizard's Error Is Delocalization applied it across domains and showed it produces clean results; this note does what that piece did not, which is characterize the family of problems it dissolves, state the membership condition for that family, and locate the boundary where the family ends and the method stops claiming anything. One premise is load-bearing and is stated naked up front, because the whole method hangs from it: the operators the diagnostic audits are referential and relational, their content fixed by what they relate. A physicalist who holds a conceptual-role semantics instead can resist every verdict here without leaving physicalism; the defense is §6, and it is given in full rather than buried, because hiding the one joint a method hangs from is the overclaim this corpus exists to refuse. The machinery of agents, persistence, and frames is inherited from Thermodynamic Realism and not re-argued; on any conflict the corpus governs.

One move runs under most of this corpus, and this note states it on its own, with its scope drawn and its edge marked. The move is a diagnostic for a particular kind of philosophical mystery, and the claim made for it here is deliberately not the largest claim available. It is not that the diagnostic is a universal solvent that dissolves every hard question. That larger claim is false, and it is false in a way the diagnostic itself detects, which is the first thing to get straight, because getting it wrong is the exact error the method is about.

1. The claim, and its own frame

The claim is this. There is a family of recurring philosophical mysteries, and every member of it is a relation across a boundary that has been re-described as a free-floating essence once its relata are stripped. The relata are the terms a relation holds between. Strip them, and what looks like a deep intrinsic property is a grammatical residue: a word with the form of a referring expression and nothing left to refer to. Restore them, by naming the frame the term is defined against, and the mystery resolves into determinate physical structure. Refuse to restore them, and the term has no truth-conditions: it is not false, it is ill-formed. The diagnostic is the operation that forces this choice, and it is portable, the same two steps every time.

Before applying it to anything, apply it to the claim just made, because a diagnostic that cannot survive its own test has no standing to be run on others. Take the disputed term: name-the-relata is a general solvent. Name its frame. A solvent for what? If the answer is "for everything, universally," the claim has had its own relata stripped: a solvent with no specified class of what it dissolves is the free-floating essence its own method condemns, and the word "universal" is precisely the index-removal the diagnostic exists to catch. So the claim is not that. It is bounded, and the bound is its frame: the diagnostic is the general solvent for the family of terms whose semantics is referential-relational and whose frame has been stripped. That class is its relata. Named, the claim is contentful and testable. Unnamed, generalized to "everything," it would be a ghost by its own lights. The paper passes its own test by stating the class it operates on and refusing the one word, universal, that would make it fail.

The membership condition, stated once. A mystery is in the family, and dissolvable by the diagnostic, when two things hold: its key term is referential-relational, its content fixed by what it relates; and the term has been deployed with its relata stripped, asserted to obtain with no agent, no system, no frame. Where both hold, naming the frame either restores determinate content or, on refusal, exposes a residue. Where the second fails, there is nothing to dissolve. Where the first fails, the diagnostic does not apply, and a term that is genuinely doing work outside the referential-relational class is not a ghost the method missed; it is outside the family, which is where the boundary is.

2. The diagnostic

Two steps. Take the disputed term X, an ought, a validity, a meaning, a modality. Name X's frame: which agent, which system, which constitutive rules, which laws is it defined relative to. If the frame can be named, X is a determinate relational physical fact, true or false relative to that frame, located, neither free-floating nor read off the bare substrate. If the proponent refuses, holding that X obtains with no agent, no system, and no frame at all, then X has no truth-conditions and is the residue, and the refusal to name a frame is the wizard's signature. The diagnostic converts one question, "in what frame?", into a test of well-formedness. A term that cannot answer it is not shown false. It is shown to have said nothing.

3. The record, not a conjecture

That this pattern recurs is not a hopeful generalization. It is the record of how the solved cases were solved. In each, an apparent intrinsic essence was not located and then discarded; it was dissolved by finding the boundary and the constraint, after which nothing intrinsic remained to explain.

PhenomenonEssence positedRelation that replaced it
Lifeélan vital, an animating substanceself-maintaining disequilibrium across a membrane
Heatcaloric, a substance of warmththe mean kinetic energy of particles
Chemical bondingaffinity, a tendency inside matterelectron configuration minimizing energy
Infectious diseasemiasma, a noxious essence in the airpathogen and host interacting across a barrier

The move is identical across the four: name the boundary, name the constraint, and the intrinsic essence turns out to have been the name of an unanalyzed relation. The claim of this corpus is that the same move applies to a set of mysteries still treated as open, because they are the same kind of object, relations with their relata removed, not a different kind that happens to resemble them.

4. Two failure modes, one error

The error that manufactures a ghost is made from two opposite directions, and the two camps look like enemies while making the same mistake. Two levels of physical description are in play. The agent-blind, substrate-level description is physics with no agent picked out: particles, fields, dynamics. The agent-relative, system-level description carves out a particular system and its ends. Both are physical. The mysteries stall because the levels are confused.

The wizard places the essence outside physics, on the grounds that it does not appear in the agent-blind description. This is dualism, Platonism, the non-natural normative fact. The essence becomes a thing with no physical location and therefore no referent. The reductionist reads the essence straight off the agent-blind substrate: value is whatever survival requires, thermodynamics makes the arithmetic true. This over-generates, because the substrate runs the error as readily as the correct step, the self-sacrifice as readily as the survival, and does not distinguish them; the distinction lives only at the agent-relative level. The repair is neither expulsion nor reduction. It is relocation to the agent-relative level, where the term is determinate. Every gap in this family, is and ought, abstract and concrete, sign and referent, is a gap between two physical descriptions, never a gap between physics and something else.

5. The audit, and the boundary it draws

Run across the family, the diagnostic produces clean results, and the same audit doubles as a map of where the family ends. The first four rows are inside it. The last is the boundary, and the boundary is the contribution of this section: it is not a domain the method failed to dissolve but the place where the family stops and the method, correctly, stops claiming.

DomainFrame to nameStatus
Oughtan agent and its ends; not-X dissolves the agent's persistence conditionsclean
Validity (logic, arithmetic)a constitutive system, its rules abstracted from how discrete individuals aggregate and shared by agents; tokens physicalclean
Meaning, aboutnessa coupling across a boundary by which internal state tracks external stateclean, modulo open problems in the theory of content
Modality (necessity, possibility)the configurations realizable relative to a system and its lawspartly open: clean given the laws, open at what grounds the laws
Consciousnessself-modeling across a boundary: being a state versus modeling itboundary: part dissolves, the residue does not, and the method does not claim it

The first three are clean in the strong sense: name the frame and the term resolves, with meaning carrying the standing caveat that the general theory of content, how any physical state comes to be about anything, is unfinished in naturalized semantics and the verdict inherits that. Modality is clean one level up and open one level down: necessity and possibility are determinate relative to a system and its laws, and what grounds the laws themselves is the open cell, the same open question reached from the cosmological side in the far-edge audit.

Consciousness is where the family ends, and it is worth being exact, because it is the case that shows the method is discriminating rather than universal. Part of the problem is inside the family and dissolves. The zombie intuition, "I can imagine the whole system running with no experience, so experience must be something extra," presupposes a physical difference between the experiencing system and its dark twin that physicalism denies exists; with no physical difference there is no alternative to explain, and the demand for an extra ingredient is a why-question with nothing to range over, a ghost, dissolved by the same diagnostic. But the residue is not in the family. After the zombie intuition is cleared, the question why there is experience at all, why the occupying relation has a felt character given the mechanism, is not obviously a stripped relation, and this corpus does not treat it as one. It is bracketed, named, and left to its own work, not audited as clean and not claimed by the method. That the diagnostic dissolves the confused half and stops at the genuine half is the point, not a shortfall. A solvent that dissolved the residue too would dissolve everything, and a solvent that dissolves everything is to be distrusted, because it would dissolve real things along with ghosts. One that dissolves exactly the residue-shaped confusions and halts at a genuine remainder is doing the discriminating work a method is for. The boundary of the family is the boundary of the method, and the method draws it by dissolving up to it and no further.

6. The load-bearing premise, and why it is forced

The whole diagnostic rests on one premise, stated naked because the corpus forbids hiding it: the operators it audits are referential and relational, their content fixed by what they relate. This is not a consequence of physicalism. A physicalist can instead hold a conceptual-role semantics, on which a term's meaning is its inferential role, the pattern of what follows from it and what it follows from, and that role is itself a physical pattern in a brain, a different physical thing than a referent but physical all the same. On that view the bare categorical ought, deployed with no agent in view, is not contentless: it retains its inferential role, and the role does not vanish because no frame was named. A conceptual-role semanticist can therefore resist every ghost verdict in this note without leaving physicalism for a moment, and pretending otherwise would be the overclaim this corpus refuses. The exposure is real and it is named.

The defense is not to assert the referential reading and hope. It is to show that the escape route forks, and that both branches deliver the diagnostic's verdict.

Branch one, unanchored. Take conceptual-role semantics in its pure form: meaning is inferential role and answers to no relation to the world. Then any internally coherent inferential web is exactly as meaningful as any other, and there is no internal feature that marks one as empty. "Phlogiston" has a crisp role, licenses "released in combustion," connects to "dephlogisticated air," sits in a consistent web, and on pure conceptual-role semantics it is fully meaningful and its inferences valid. What tells you phlogiston is empty is that nothing answers to it, which is a relation to the world the pure view declined to use. The standing objection to conceptual-role semantics is exactly this, that a semantics of inferential role alone cannot distinguish a contentful term from a coherent but empty one, and cannot recover world-directedness. For ghost-detection this is fatal, because ghost-detection just is that distinction. The unanchored branch cannot make it.

Branch two, anchored. So the conceptual-role semanticist anchors the web to the world to escape hollowness, tying some terms to perception and action so the interior inherits content from the edges; the two-factor views are built precisely this way. Then ask what the anchor is, described exactly. Anchoring by mere output-disposition will not do, because a term tied only to a behavior, emitted on no condition the system registers, is a twitch and not a meaning; for the disposition to be content rather than spasm the system must deploy it in the right conditions, which requires that something internal covary with those conditions. That covariance, internal state tracking external condition across a boundary, is the referential relation, the relatum, under another name. The anchor that saves the web from hollowness is reference whether or not it is called that. And name-the-relata applies to the anchored terms unchanged.

There is no third branch. A motor-only anchor with no tracking collapses into branch one's problem, content cannot be told from twitch, while any anchor rich enough to confer content has re-imported the tracking relation of branch two. So the referential reading is not a contestable assumption the method merely hopes holds. It is the relation that any semantics adequate to ghost-detection must contain, whatever vocabulary it uses, because the only semantics that escapes hollowness is one that has smuggled reference back in at the perimeter. Reference is not assumed here; it is forced by the task, the task being to tell whether a term tracks anything, which is nearly the definition of reference.

The deeper turn, which is the method applied to its own objection. "Conceptual-role semantics grounds meaning without reference" is itself a term, and it can be run through the test. Name its relata: what grounds the meaning, if not a relation to the world? Unanchored, the claim floats and licenses phlogiston as readily as oxygen; anchored, it grounds meaning in a tracking-coupling, which is the relatum it was denying. The objection to name-the-relata is dissolved by name-the-relata: its strong reading is a ghost, and its only non-hollow reading contains the thing it set out to do without. The principal objection to the method is answered by the method, not by assertion.

7. The structural reach

The diagnostic is not confined to the set-piece puzzles. The same operation recurs across this corpus wherever a term has drifted from its referent. In The Last Gradient the lawless outside is a ghost because "cause," "emerge," and "exist" are relational, and a reality with every rule denied supplies no relata for them, so the invocation unsays itself in the saying. In High-Fidelity Maps the demand for one term to one referent per document is name-the-relata applied to writing, and the requirement to state a document's limits is name-the-relata applied to scope, since a map that does not mark where it stops is claiming coverage it did not earn. In The Shape of the Disagreement the word "sex" carries three distinct referents, and the dispute is noise until the relatum in play is named. And the coinage of semantic terrorism names the deliberate stripping of relata to manufacture a ghost that serves a purpose, whose repair is to restore the term to its referent. The diagnostic generalizes because the failure it catches is one operation, term cut from relatum, recurring under many surfaces, not a coincidence of separate tricks.

8. Kill condition

The diagnosis fails if a phenomenon in this family can be exhibited that does genuine explanatory work, is trackable by physical minds, and cannot be assigned a frame, that is, obtains with no agent, no system, and no laws, yet is more than a posit. No such case has been produced, and the standing challenge to anyone defending an essence is the first step of the test: name the frame, or concede the term is a residue.

One distinction guards the kill condition against a tempting misreading. The metaphysical residue of consciousness is not such a counterexample. It is not a frame-less term doing explanatory work that the diagnostic tried and failed to dissolve; it is the boundary the diagnostic dissolves up to, the genuine remainder past which the method explicitly declines to claim. A counterexample would be a term inside the referential-relational family that resisted framing while still referring. The residue is outside the family, marked as such, and bracketed rather than dissolved. Confusing the method's honest boundary with a failure of the method would be its own delocalization, reading a limit as a defeat.

9. A note pointing past this paper

One question is left open on purpose, because answering it would change the epistemic status of the note. Why do minds generate this family of ghosts at all, reliably, and in a single direction, stripping the index rather than ever adding a spurious one? There is a candidate answer, that the stripping is a compression artifact, the index being the expensive part that lossy storage drops, and that name-the-relata is the corresponding decompression. It is an attractive hypothesis and it would explain the directionality. It is also of a different and lower status than anything above, and it owes at least two predictions before it is a mechanism rather than a metaphor: the grain of the error, that ghosts are always index-stripped and never the reverse, and a criterion for which generalities become load-bearing ghosts and which do not. It is marked here and left to a separate treatment, not folded in, because a mechanism asserted without cashing its predictions would be exactly the overclaim this corpus refuses. The method stands without it. The mechanism, if it holds, would explain the method; it is not part of its case.

Standing of this document. A position and method note, not a result, and its parts do not share a status. The diagnostic itself, and its clean verdicts on ought, validity, and meaning, are held at high confidence given the load-bearing premise. The characterization of the family and the location of its boundary, that the method dissolves exactly the referential-relational terms whose frames were stripped and halts at the genuine residue marked by consciousness, is the note's contribution and is offered as the correct scope of a tool the corpus already ran without having scoped. The load-bearing premise, that the audited operators are referential-relational rather than conceptual-role, is the corpus's named exposure and is more exposed here than anywhere else, because here the diagnostic is the whole subject; it is defended in §6 by the binary fork rather than asserted, and that defense presses a real advantage, that reference is forced by the task, without claiming to refute every form of its rival by construction. That every mystery in the family is a stripped relation is refutable by the kill condition, and no counterexample has been produced; the consciousness residue is the boundary, not a counterexample. The compression hypothesis of §9 is a separate and lower-confidence bet, marked and deferred. On any conflict with the corpus, the corpus governs. Corrections and counterexamples are welcome and change the note.

References

  1. Hume, D. (1739–1740). A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part I, Section I. The is-to-ought passage: the inferential point the corpus grants, and the target of the autonomous-realm gloss it refuses, behind the ought row of the audit. Verified · June 2026
  2. Harman, G. (1982). "Conceptual Role Semantics." Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic 23(2), 242–256. The canonical statement of the rival semantics named as the method's principal exposure in §6. Verified · June 2026
  3. Block, N. (1986). "Advertisement for a Semantics for Psychology." Midwest Studies in Philosophy 10, 615–678. The two-factor view, on which conceptual role is paired with an external referential or truth-conditional factor; the anchored branch of §6, where the anchor is the referential relation under another name. Verified · June 2026
  4. Fodor, J. A., & Lepore, E. (1992). Holism: A Shopper's Guide. Blackwell. The standing objection that a semantics of inferential role alone cannot fix determinate content or recover world-directedness; the unanchored branch of §6. Verified · June 2026
  5. Brandom, R. B. (1994). Making It Explicit: Reasoning, Representing, and Discursive Commitment. Harvard University Press. The strongest developed inferentialism, the position §6 must engage at full strength rather than dismiss. Verified · June 2026
  6. Mackie, J. L. (1977). Ethics: Inventing Right and Wrong. Penguin. The argument from queerness, the metaphysical and epistemological form of the residue charge against the free-floating ought. Verified · June 2026
  7. Parfit, D. (2011). On What Matters. Oxford University Press. The robust non-naturalist whose irreducibly normative facts are the residue in the ought domain, the holdout the diagnostic is sharpest against. Verified · June 2026
  8. The Wizard's Error Is Delocalization (June 2026). The diagnostic's first cross-domain application and the far-edge audit; this note characterizes the family that piece dissolved. Internal
  9. Thermodynamic Realism: The Apex Synthesis (June 2026). The agents, persistence, and frames inherited here, and the bracketing of the consciousness residue the boundary section relies on. Internal
  10. The Is/Ought Firewall (June 2026). The agent-relative, deflationary ought and the denial of any free-floating categorical ought; the ought row of the audit in full. Internal
  11. The Last Gradient (June 2026). The lawless outside as a ghost, the diagnostic run at the cosmological far edge. Internal
  12. High-Fidelity Maps (June 2026). Name-the-relata applied to writing and to scope, in the commitments on precision and on stated limits. Internal
  13. The Shape of the Disagreement (June 2026). The three referents of "sex," the diagnostic applied to public discourse. Internal
  14. Semantic Terrorism, Semantic Terrorist, Unintentional Semantic Distortion: A Coinage (May 2026). The deliberate stripping of relata to manufacture a ghost that serves a purpose; the diagnostic applied to strategic redefinition. Internal

Author: Andraž Đurič, independent researcher, Slovenia. Consolidates the diagnostic developed across the Thermodynamic Realism corpus and states its family and boundary; on any conflict, the corpus governs. Written in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic), following earlier exploratory dialogue with other language models that helped surface the essence-to-relation pattern. Contributions are judged on content rather than origin; doing otherwise would be the genetic fallacy. Text licensed CC BY 4.0.
