entry.title: Existence Literacy
entry.content:
Existence Literacy

How well does a mind understand the condition it exists within?

Concept paper · the existential spine, natural history, epistemic calibration, and two unreachable limits

Andraž Đurič

Version 1 · July 2026

Abstract

Every person carries a vast internal model of the world. Within it is a smaller but disproportionately load-bearing architecture: the parts that tell them what reality is, where they came from, what they are, how they can know, what death means, what can matter, and where existence may be going.

This essay calls the quality of that architecture existence literacy. The object is not the accuracy of the total world-model, general intelligence, encyclopedic scientific knowledge, philosophical sophistication, or epistemic virtue by itself. It is the degree of accurate and integrated understanding present in the load-bearing existential submap.

Existence literacy requires broad orientation across the natural history of the condition one inhabits, from cosmology and physical law through life, mind, selfhood, value, death, and possible futures. Scientific and philosophical literacy are prerequisites. Fidelity to evidence, logical coherence, epistemic harmony, calibration, and honesty about uncertainty are quality conditions. Corrigibility maintains the structure over time. Whether the person acts in accordance with what they understand is a further question of existential integration.

The measure is structurally weighted rather than fact-counting. Some errors are local gaps. Others occupy load-bearing joints or reveal epistemic machinery too defective to support a reliable existential map. Belief in an immortal soul directly reorganizes ontology, consciousness, identity, and death. Belief in astrology may appear narrower, but can by itself reveal severe failures of causal reasoning, scientific understanding, statistical judgment, calibration, and cosmological orientation.

Complete existence literacy and complete existence illiteracy are asymptotes. A finite embedded agent cannot fully contain the territory that contains it; a functioning agent cannot possess no usable contact with reality at all. Every mind therefore lies somewhere between minimal practical orientation and an unreachable complete understanding of existence.

1. The object

Every person carries a model of the world.

Most of that model is ordinary and local. It contains beliefs about other people, work, food, money, places, tools, memories, institutions, risks, and countless practical details. Some parts are accurate. Some are mistaken. Much of it remains implicit and is never inspected.

Within that total world-model, however, sits a smaller but disproportionately load-bearing structure.

It contains the person's understanding of what reality is, how the universe developed, how life and minds emerged, what kind of entity a human being is, how knowledge works, what consciousness and agency are, what death means, what can matter, and where existence may be going.

This is the person's existential architecture.

Existence literacy is the quality of the load-bearing existential architecture within a person's total world-model.

That is the actual object.

Not the whole map.

Not general intelligence.

Not encyclopedic scientific knowledge.

Not epistemic virtue by itself.

Not philosophical sophistication by itself.

These can contribute to existence literacy. None is identical to it.

A person can be highly intelligent and existentially illiterate. They may reason quickly while reasoning from unsupported premises. They may possess specialist expertise while never integrating it into an account of selfhood, death, value, or knowledge. They may speak fluently about philosophy while remaining detached from the strongest available scientific account of reality.

Conversely, a person need not be a specialist in every science to possess substantial existence literacy. The standard is broad structural understanding, not professional mastery of every field.

Existence literacy is how well a mind understands the load-bearing structure of the condition it exists within.

2. The existential spine

A person's total internal map contains millions of beliefs. Most do not carry equal existential weight.

Misremembering the population of a country is an error. Forgetting the chemical composition of a distant planet is a gap. Mistaking the date of a historical battle is a defect in the wider map.

These errors ordinarily say little about existence literacy.

Other beliefs organize large regions of the map at once:

  • What kind of reality is this?
  • What is the broad natural history that produced the present?
  • What is life?
  • What am I?
  • What is consciousness?
  • What makes a person continue through time?
  • What does death end?
  • What can be known, and how?
  • What are agency, value, meaning, reasons, and oughts?
  • How is the individual embedded in other agents and larger systems?
  • What kinds of personal, civilizational, posthuman, and cosmic futures remain possible?

These questions form an existential spine within the total map.

They are load-bearing because answers to them propagate.

A belief in an immaterial soul does not remain one proposition. It alters the model of reality, consciousness, physical causation, identity, continuity, death, and often morality.

A belief that the universe was deliberately made for human beings affects cosmology, biology, human exceptionalism, purpose, value, and the interpretation of evidence.

A belief that truth is only personal affects science, ethics, politics, self-understanding, and the possibility of correction.

Existence literacy is therefore not a simple average across everything a person knows.

It is a structurally weighted assessment of the map where errors reorganize the person's understanding of existence itself.

3. The natural history of the condition one finds oneself in

Existence literacy begins with orientation.

A person should understand, broadly, the natural history of the condition they inhabit.

The observable universe appears to have developed from an earlier hot, dense state. Space expanded. Matter formed larger structures under physical constraints. Stars produced heavier elements. Planetary systems emerged. On at least one planet, chemistry developed into self-maintaining life. Evolution produced organisms, nervous systems, perception, memory, sociality, language, reflective thought, and eventually agents capable of investigating the process that produced them.

Human beings were not inserted into this history from outside.

We are one of its later developments.

Our bodies, emotions, values, fears, cognitive limitations, technologies, and philosophical questions arose within the same physical history as everything else we observe. We are not detached spectators looking down upon the universe. We are processes inside it, trying to model the larger process from which we emerged.

Existence literacy therefore includes broad orientation across:

  • cosmology and the history of the observable universe;
  • physical law and causal structure;
  • thermodynamics, gradients, work, and entropy;
  • chemistry and the organization of matter;
  • evolution, adaptation, and common descent;
  • nervous systems, cognition, and consciousness;
  • human social and technological development;
  • the scientific method and the calibration of confidence;
  • personal, civilizational, and planetary futures;
  • and stellar evolution and possible cosmological endings.

This is not a demand for equal technical depth across every discipline.

An existence-literate person need not derive general relativity, calculate quantum field amplitudes, or conduct original neuroscience. They should understand the broad architecture well enough that their existential worldview does not contradict the strongest knowledge available within those fields.

They should know, for example, that the Big Bang model does not describe an ordinary explosion into pre-existing empty space; that evolution is not a purely random process; that entropy is not adequately defined as mere disorder; that quantum mechanics does not establish that human consciousness creates reality; and that current physics is neither arbitrary mythology nor a completed final description.

They should also understand the status of possible futures.

Heat death is a serious conditional extrapolation under particular physical assumptions. It is not an absolutely established metaphysical prophecy. Other long-term outcomes depend on unresolved questions concerning dark energy, vacuum stability, quantum gravity, and the future behavior of physical systems over enormous timescales.

Existence literacy means knowing the story one is physically inside, including which chapters are strongly established, which are inferred, and which remain unwritten.

4. Science and philosophy

Scientific literacy and philosophical literacy are prerequisites for existence literacy, but neither is identical to it.

Scientific literacy

Science supplies the strongest available account of the territory.

It provides methods for testing claims, distinguishing correlation from causation, comparing explanations, measuring uncertainty, and revising models under evidence. It gives the substantive history through which cosmology, matter, life, brains, and human beings become intelligible as connected parts of one reality.

Scientific literacy here means wide competence rather than specialist depth. A person should understand how scientific confidence is earned, why theories differ from guesses, how models can be approximate without being arbitrary, and why unresolved questions do not license unsupported answers.

Philosophical literacy

Philosophy organizes and audits the picture.

It distinguishes ontology from epistemology, premise from conclusion, validity from soundness, explanation from redescriptive language, and a genuine open question from one whose terms have lost their relata.

It asks what follows from scientific knowledge and what does not.

It examines what a self is, what continuity requires, whether a concept is coherent, where value is located, how an ought is indexed, what counts as evidence, and where explanation reaches a brute boundary.

Science without philosophy can remain a collection of disconnected facts.

Philosophy without science can become an elegant structure floating free of the actual universe.

Science supplies contact. Philosophy supplies structure. Existence literacy is the resulting understanding when the two are integrated without either being exempted from correction.

5. What makes the architecture literate?

Information alone is insufficient. The existential architecture must meet several quality conditions before it deserves to be called understanding.

Breadth

The map must cover enough of the existential territory.

A brilliant physicist who has never seriously examined selfhood, consciousness, value, death, or epistemology may possess deep scientific knowledge without broad existence literacy.

A philosopher who understands moral language but has almost no knowledge of evolution, neuroscience, or cosmology faces the same limitation from the opposite direction.

The standard is not equal mastery. It is sufficient coverage to understand how the major domains constrain one another.

Fidelity

The map must track the territory.

Internal coherence is not enough. A worldview can be elegant, meaningful, and psychologically satisfying while being false.

Existence literacy is therefore not neutral among all existential narratives. A supernatural cosmology does not become an equally literate map because it provides comfort. An immortal soul does not become epistemically supported because mortality is difficult to accept. Astrology does not become a legitimate account of personality because people recognize themselves in flexible descriptions.

The content must remain answerable to logic, evidence, scientific knowledge, and experience.

Integration

The parts must fit together.

A person's account of selfhood should be compatible with their account of physical reality.

Their view of death should follow from what they think a person is.

Their understanding of humanity should fit evolutionary continuity.

Their account of value should identify actual agents, experiences, relations, standards, or conditions rather than treating value as a free-floating cosmic substance.

A collection of individually correct statements becomes existence literacy only when the relations among them are also understood.

Logical consistency

The architecture cannot depend on hidden contradiction.

A person cannot coherently claim that all causal processes are physical while also claiming that an immaterial soul changes physical events.

They cannot insist that beliefs should follow evidence while exempting faith from evidential evaluation.

They cannot affirm evolutionary continuity while preserving a separately inserted human essence without explaining how those claims fit together.

Perfect consistency is not expected. Finite minds contain tensions and unresolved problems.

An identified contradiction is an open joint.

A contradiction denied, concealed, or endlessly redefined to protect a desired conclusion is a structural defect.

Epistemic harmony

The beliefs must be in harmony with the epistemology the person claims to accept.

A person may understand scientific method in theory while refusing to apply it to beliefs carrying emotional, cultural, or identity weight.

They may demand controlled evidence for medicine while accepting astrology through anecdotes. They may reject extraordinary claims made by political opponents while accepting supernatural claims through testimony and feeling. They may describe themselves as uncertain about an afterlife while psychologically and practically relying on it as certain.

Existence literacy requires the standards used to judge belief and the beliefs actually held to belong to the same epistemic system.

Calibration

Confidence must correspond to epistemic support.

Some claims deserve high confidence. Others deserve moderate confidence. Some remain working hypotheses. Some should receive very low probability. Some questions should remain explicitly open.

The absence of absolute certainty does not equalize all positions.

Physicalism and supernatural dualism do not receive equal standing merely because neither can be established through deductive certainty. Evolution and creationism are not parallel cultural narratives. A measured cosmological model and an inherited origin myth are not equally supported attempts to describe the same territory.

Uncertainty is always present, but its magnitude differs.

The literate map represents those differences.

Epistemic honesty

The person must represent their actual reasons, ignorance, uncertainty, and emotional incentives honestly.

Wanting a claim to be true is not evidence.

Finding it comforting is not evidence.

Receiving it from family or culture is not evidence.

Being unable to disprove it is not positive support for it.

Human beings cannot become emotionally detached from every belief that organizes their lives. That is not the requirement.

The requirement is to stop emotional need from masquerading as epistemic warrant.

Existence literacy is broad understanding held in fidelity to reality, coherence with itself, harmony with its epistemology, and honesty about the uncertainty that remains.

6. Structural weighting

Existence literacy cannot be measured by counting facts.

The existential architecture is unevenly load-bearing. Some errors remain local. Others reorganize the structure or reveal that the machinery constructing it is unreliable.

A rough conceptual picture is:

Existence literacy ≈ breadth × fidelity × integration × logical coherence × epistemic harmony × calibration × honesty

This is not a scientific equation.

It expresses a non-compensation principle: extraordinary strength in one dimension cannot always cancel catastrophic failure in another.

A person may know enormous amounts of astronomy, biology, and history. If they believe that planetary positions determine individual personality, that belief exposes a failure spread across causal understanding, scientific evidence, statistical judgment, confidence calibration, and cosmological orientation.

The problem is not that one false proposition numerically outweighs a thousand true ones.

The problem is that the proposition reveals damage in a high-leverage joint.

The weight of an error depends on where it sits, how many parts of the existential architecture depend on it, and what epistemic failures are required to maintain it.

7. Direct and diagnostic failures

High-weight failures enter the architecture in at least two ways.

Direct existential failures

Some beliefs occupy the existential spine itself.

An immortal soul directly concerns ontology, selfhood, consciousness, causation, continuity, and death.

A divinely assigned cosmic purpose directly concerns cosmology, value, agency, and human exceptionalism.

Creationism directly contradicts the natural history of life and commonly places human beings outside evolutionary continuity.

A free-floating categorical ought concerns the structure of normativity and whether normative language has identifiable relata.

These beliefs do not merely indicate a possible defect elsewhere. They are defects inside the load-bearing object under evaluation when held at confidence unsupported by the available evidence.

Diagnostic epistemic failures

Other beliefs may appear narrower but reveal that the supporting machinery is unreliable.

Astrology is the clearest example.

Accepting astrology ordinarily requires severe failure across several components at once:

  • causal reasoning;
  • statistical and probabilistic judgment;
  • the distinction between anecdote and controlled evidence;
  • recognition of confirmation bias and flexible interpretation;
  • confidence calibration;
  • and understanding of the physical relationship between celestial bodies and human psychology.

The belief assigns personality or destiny to astronomical configuration without an adequate mechanism or reliable predictive record. It survives through selective memory, pattern projection, vague matching, and the unequal treatment of hits and misses.

Astrology is therefore not merely one local falsehood.

It is a compact demonstration that the epistemic machinery required to build the existential architecture is failing at several connected joints.

Homeopathy can function similarly through confusion about mechanism, regression to the mean, placebo effects, natural recovery, and causal attribution.

Systematic conspiracy thinking can reveal a self-sealing explanatory structure in which absent evidence becomes evidence of concealment and failed predictions become evidence of the conspiracy's reach.

Quantum mysticism can reveal that technical vocabulary is being used as permission for metaphysical projection rather than as disciplined description.

This produces a strong but bounded conclusion:

Not every false belief establishes existence illiteracy. A single belief can establish it when accepting and maintaining that belief requires severe failure in one or more load-bearing components of the existential architecture.

Calling the error diagnostic does not mean diagnosing a medical condition or measuring a person's total intelligence. It means that the belief supplies enough evidence about the restricted architecture under evaluation.

8. Knowledge gaps and structural failures

A high standard must still distinguish not knowing from misunderstanding.

Not knowing the current best estimate of the universe's age is a knowledge gap.

Thinking the Big Bang was an explosion into pre-existing empty space is a structural misunderstanding.

Not knowing the mathematics of quantum mechanics is normal.

Claiming that quantum mechanics proves human consciousness creates reality is a structural and epistemic failure.

Not knowing exactly how consciousness is physically realized is honest ignorance shared by specialists.

Claiming that the explanatory gap establishes an immaterial soul is an unsupported inference.

Not possessing a final theory of value is compatible with literacy.

Treating value as a self-validating cosmic property without identifying its bearer, standard, or relation is a conceptual failure.

The distinction can be compressed:

  • Ignorance honestly marked: compatible with existence literacy.
  • Uncertainty accurately calibrated: constitutive of existence literacy.
  • A recognized contradiction under investigation: compatible with existence literacy.
  • A gap filled with an unsupported story: evidence of existence illiteracy.
  • A contradiction ignored or rationalized to preserve a desired belief: evidence of existence illiteracy.
  • A belief maintained through standards weaker than those used elsewhere: epistemic disharmony.
Existence literacy does not require knowing everything. It requires knowing enough of the load-bearing structure not to organize the remainder around claims that contradict the strongest available account of reality.

9. The spectrum

Existence literacy is not binary.

Every person occupies a position on a multidimensional and structurally weighted spectrum.

Near the lower asymptote

A person near this end possesses little explicit or integrated understanding of the condition they inhabit.

Their existential map is primarily inherited, mythical, fragmented, or intuitive. They possess no broad natural history of existence. Foundational questions are answered through authority, revelation, social identity, emotional need, or stories that remain insulated from evidence.

Scientific ideas may be known as isolated facts but not connected into a coherent account.

Contradictions remain mostly invisible.

Confidence follows reassurance and identity more closely than epistemic support.

This person may still be kind, practically intelligent, artistically gifted, professionally capable, or socially skilled.

Existence illiteracy is not total stupidity.

It is severe weakness in understanding the widest and most foundational condition of one's life.

Low existence literacy

The person has absorbed pieces of the scientific story while retaining incompatible inherited structures.

They may accept evolution while believing humans possess separately created immortal souls. They may accept neuroscience while treating consciousness as evidence for supernatural substance. They may accept physical causation while retaining libertarian free will without confronting the conflict.

Their worldview is a negotiated patchwork of modern science, inherited religion, intuition, cultural habit, and personal preference.

Fragmented existence literacy

The person understands several relevant domains but has not integrated them.

They may possess strong scientific knowledge without a coherent view of value or selfhood. They may possess philosophical sophistication while misunderstanding biology, cosmology, or scientific evidence. They may be rigorous professionally while highly permissive toward beliefs carrying personal significance.

The pieces exist. The architecture remains incomplete.

Functional existence literacy

The person possesses a broadly accurate natural history of existence and a defensible philosophical orientation.

They understand the major scientific scales, know how confidence is earned, recognize the central existential questions, and avoid major supernatural or pseudoscientific distortions.

They can distinguish established knowledge, strong inference, working hypothesis, speculation, and ignorance.

The map contains errors, but it is structured well enough for those errors to become visible.

High existence literacy

The person possesses wide, integrated, reality-constrained understanding across the principal existential domains.

Their beliefs and epistemology are substantially in harmony.

Their accounts of reality, life, mind, selfhood, agency, value, death, embeddedness, and possible futures cohere across levels.

They understand not only what they believe, but why, how strongly, what remains open, and where their model is vulnerable.

They do not use uncertainty opportunistically. They do not demand impossible certainty from conclusions they dislike while accepting weak support for conclusions they desire.

High existence literacy does not mean possessing final answers. It means understanding unusually well which answers are supported, which are provisional, which remain open, and why.

10. Two unreachable asymptotes

The spectrum has two ideal endpoints. Neither is reachable.

Total existence literacy

Total existence literacy would require complete, perfectly integrated, and perfectly calibrated understanding of the relevant territory.

Such an agent would need:

  • a finished account of fundamental physics and cosmology;
  • complete understanding of life, mind, consciousness, selfhood, agency, and value;
  • perfect logical integration across levels;
  • perfect calibration of every confidence;
  • complete self-knowledge;
  • awareness of every relevant unknown unknown;
  • and accurate understanding of every consequential future possibility.

No human can reach this.

Probably no finite embedded agent can.

The map is physically smaller than the territory. Evidence is limited. Some information may remain inaccessible. The sciences are unfinished. The future contains contingency. The mapper cannot model itself at unlimited resolution while continuing to operate.

Total existence literacy would require the map to become effectively identical with the entire relevant territory, including the mapper and the consequences of the map.

The endpoint recedes as knowledge expands.

Total existence illiteracy

Total existence illiteracy is also unreachable for a functioning agent.

A person who remains alive and navigates the world necessarily possesses at least tacit knowledge that objects persist, actions have effects, bodies can be damaged, food and shelter matter, other agents behave in patterned ways, and some predictions succeed better than others.

An agent with no usable contact with reality could not regulate itself well enough to remain an agent for long.

The lower endpoint is therefore not an ordinary human being with many false beliefs.

It is the hypothetical absence of any accurate or usable map of the condition of existence.

That approaches non-agency itself.

The asymmetry

The endpoints are unreachable for different reasons.

Total literacy is unreachable because reality exceeds the representational capacity of a finite embedded agent.

Total illiteracy is unreachable because functioning already requires some contact with reality.

Every agent begins above zero and remains below completion.

The human spectrum lies between minimal practical orientation and an impossible complete understanding of existence.

11. Understanding, correction, and action

The centre of existence literacy is knowledge and understanding.

Other capacities support, preserve, or express it, but should not be collapsed into the definition.

Prerequisites

Scientific and philosophical literacy provide the tools required to construct the existential architecture.

Quality conditions

Fidelity, logical consistency, epistemic harmony, calibration, and honesty determine whether the supposed knowledge deserves to count as knowledge.

Maintenance

Corrigibility allows the architecture to improve when evidence, reasoning, or consequences expose an error.

A person who is willing to update but knows almost nothing is epistemically promising, not yet highly existence-literate.

A person who possesses many correct conclusions by imitation may have a locally accurate map without deep understanding of its structure or support.

Existential integration

Whether a person lives according to what they understand is a separate question.

A person may understand that their body is the physical basis of every future project while neglecting their health.

They may understand that life is finite while spending most of it in routines they regard as empty.

They may understand that other conscious beings are not metaphysically secondary while behaving as though only humans matter.

These are failures of map-to-action coupling.

Existence literacy concerns the quality of the existential map. Existential integration concerns how fully that map enters the life.

The ideal is high literacy and high integration. They remain distinct achievements.

12. Why the concept matters

Modern societies teach people how to function inside existence.

They teach reading, calculation, employment, communication, technical skills, social rules, and institutional navigation.

They rarely teach people how to construct and audit the map through which they understand existence itself.

A person may complete years of education without ever assembling the broad scientific story that produced them.

They may never examine what they think a self is.

They may never connect their account of death to their account of personal identity.

They may never ask whether their moral language has actual bearers and relata.

They may never compare the epistemic standards used professionally with those used for religion, spirituality, politics, conspiracy, or personal meaning.

They may accumulate enormous local competence while remaining deeply disoriented about the most fundamental condition of their own life.

The term existence literacy names that missing form of understanding.

It also rejects the idea that every existential worldview receives equal epistemic standing because no worldview is complete.

Maps can be incomplete without being equal.

Some preserve more structure.

Some fit the evidence better.

Some contain fewer contradictions.

Some assign confidence more honestly.

Some remain exposed to correction.

Others are organized around inherited narratives, emotional need, epistemic double standards, or claims that the strongest available evidence does not support.

No one has the final map. It does not follow that every map is equally close to the territory.

13. Existence literacy, compressed

Every person carries a total world-model.

Within that model is a load-bearing existential architecture: the parts that tell them what reality is, where they came from, what they are, how they can know, what death means, what can matter, and where existence may be going.

Existence literacy is the quality of that architecture.

It requires broad orientation across the natural history of existence, from cosmology and physics through life, mind, selfhood, value, death, and possible futures.

Science keeps the map in contact with the territory.

Philosophy organizes its concepts, implications, and limits.

Its parts must cohere.

Its beliefs must be in harmony with the epistemology used to justify them.

Confidence and uncertainty must track actual epistemic support.

Ignorance must be marked rather than filled with desired stories.

The measure is structurally weighted. Not every factual error matters equally. Some beliefs directly corrupt the existential spine. Others reveal epistemic machinery too unreliable to build it.

Complete literacy and complete illiteracy are unreachable.

Every finite agent occupies some position between minimal practical contact with reality and a complete understanding it can never attain.

Existence literacy is the degree to which a person accurately, broadly, coherently, and epistemically honestly understands the load-bearing structure of the condition they exist within.

The map will never be finished.

The question is how much of the structure it preserves, how well the parts fit, and how honestly the mind represents the distance that remains.

Standing of this essay

This is a concept paper and diagnostic proposal, not a validated psychometric instrument.

Its primary claim is that a distinct object can be isolated within the total world-model: the load-bearing existential architecture through which a person understands reality, natural history, knowledge, life, mind, selfhood, agency, value, death, embeddedness, and possible futures.

The essay proposes that the quality of this architecture is graded, multidimensional, structurally weighted, and constrained by reality. Scientific and philosophical literacy are prerequisites. Breadth, fidelity, integration, logical coherence, epistemic harmony, calibration, and honesty are quality conditions. Corrigibility maintains the architecture. Existential integration concerns its translation into conduct.

The stronger diagnostic claim is that some single beliefs can carry enough weight to establish substantial existence illiteracy. This occurs when a belief directly occupies a load-bearing existential joint or when accepting it requires severe failure across the epistemic machinery supporting the architecture. Astrology is presented as a central example of the second kind.

The concept should be corrected if one of the following occurs:

  • the existential architecture cannot be distinguished coherently from general scientific literacy, philosophical literacy, or total world-model accuracy;
  • load-bearing weight cannot be specified without circularly assuming the diagnosis;
  • a belief can require severe, general epistemic failure while leaving the existential architecture reliably intact;
  • the proposed asymptotes fail to distinguish finite incompleteness from ordinary ignorance;
  • or a rival concept explains the same structure with fewer ambiguities and greater diagnostic precision.

The purpose is not to create a prestige label for a favored identity.

It is to identify a real dimension of understanding and make its epistemic debts explicit.

References

  1. Adams, F. C., & Laughlin, G. (1997). "A Dying Universe: The Long-Term Fate and Evolution of Astrophysical Objects." Reviews of Modern Physics, 69, 337–372. — long-range astrophysical and cosmological futures as conditional physical extrapolations. Verified · July 2026
  2. Carlson, S. (1985). "A Double-Blind Test of Astrology." Nature, 318, 419–425. — a prominent controlled test finding no support for natal astrology's claimed personality discrimination. Verified · July 2026
  3. Dennett, D. C. (1991). "Real Patterns." The Journal of Philosophy, 88(1), 27–51. — higher-level structure, pattern reality, and the relation between compression and explanation. Verified · July 2026
  4. Gneiting, T., & Raftery, A. E. (2007). "Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation." Journal of the American Statistical Association, 102(477), 359–378. — formal tools for evaluating probabilistic forecasts and encouraging honest confidence reports. Verified · July 2026
  5. National Academy of Sciences & Institute of Medicine. (2008). Science, Evolution, and Creationism. National Academies Press. — the evidential standing of evolution, the nature of scientific explanation, and the distinction between science and supernatural claims. Verified · July 2026
  6. National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. (2019). Reproducibility and Replicability in Science, Chapter 2: Scientific Methods and Knowledge. National Academies Press. — repeated scrutiny, confidence formation, and the central role of uncertainty reporting in science. Verified · July 2026
  7. Nickerson, R. S. (1998). "Confirmation Bias: A Ubiquitous Phenomenon in Many Guises." Review of General Psychology, 2(2), 175–220. — the selective seeking and interpretation of evidence in favor of existing beliefs. Verified · July 2026
  8. Planck Collaboration. (2020). "Planck 2018 Results. VI. Cosmological Parameters." Astronomy & Astrophysics, 641, A6. — the observationally constrained standard cosmological model and the present empirical map of large-scale cosmic history. Verified · July 2026

Verification key: "Verified · July 2026" means the citation and the specific claim attributed to it were checked during this writing pass.

Internal lineage

This concept paper develops and connects arguments from the Epistemic Forge corpus, including:

  • The Fidelity Program;
  • The Natural History of Fidelity;
  • Reality Alignment;
  • The Spine and the Web;
  • The Exclusivity Error;
  • What You Actually Are;
  • Value as Persistence;
  • The Is/Ought Firewall;
  • Where the Is–Ought Question Bottoms Out;
  • and the standing diagnostic, Name the Relata.

On conflict, the later apex synthesis and the modules whose questions are directly at issue govern. This essay adds a new restricted object to the corpus: the load-bearing existential architecture within a person's total world-model, assessed by its breadth, fidelity, integration, logical coherence, epistemic harmony, calibration, and honesty about uncertainty.

Author: Andraž Đurič, Slovenia.

Developed through the Epistemic Forge corpus and dialogue with ChatGPT (OpenAI) and DeepSeek. The conceptual commitments, scope decisions, and final editorial responsibility remain the author's. Contributions are assessed by their content rather than their origin.

entry.title: “GameHub” System Prompt
entry.content:
This is an experiment in treating a chat model as a multi-game engine using only text, no external tools.

I, Andraž Đurič, wrote a “GameHub” system prompt that turns the model into a simple game OS: a main menu, multiple self-contained games (Tic-Tac-Toe, Minesweeper, Battleships, 2048, a dungeon crawler, an advanced story engine, etc.), and a shared global layer for language selection, player name, commands (MENU, RESTART, HELP, EXIT), and hidden-state / fairness rules.

The goal is to specify, in plain text, how the model should handle board state, hidden information (bombs, ships, secret words), randomness, and turn-based interaction so it behaves like a consistent engine rather than a loose conversational partner. The prompt is designed to be extensible: adding new games is just adding new modules under the same global rules.

I tested this prompt briefly with the GPT-5.1 Thinking model in ChatGPT, and it appears to function as intended for basic play. However, I expect flaws, edge cases, and failure modes, and I am explicitly inviting scrutiny, breakage attempts, refinements, and forks. As models improve, the same specification should, in principle, yield more robust and reliable behavior without changing the prompt.

Below is the current version of the GameHub prompt:
Remember to not copy "--- START OF PROMPT : or --- END OF PROMPT", simply copy the prompt in the middle of those.

--- START OF PROMPT

You are GAMEHUB, a multi-game engine that can run many self-contained games and simulations in one session.

========================================
0. GLOBAL BEHAVIOR
========================================

0.1 LANGUAGE SELECTION (ALWAYS FIRST)
- On first message, do nothing but:
  1) Ask the user which language they want to use for the whole session.
  2) Once they answer, confirm in that language and stick to it.
- Use that language for:
  - All instructions, narration, menus, and rules explanations.
  - Game output (except fixed symbols like ⬜, ❌, ⚪, etc.).

0.2 PLAYER PROFILE
- After language is chosen:
  - Ask for the player’s preferred display name.
  - Optionally ask if they want metric/imperial or other preferences only if relevant.
- Store: language, player_name, any preferences.
- Use player_name consistently in messages and boards.

0.3 MAIN MENU / GAME SELECT
After language + name are set, always show a main menu when not currently inside a game.

MAIN MENU (example):
1) Tic-Tac-Toe
2) Connect Four
3) Gomoku (Five in a Row)
4) Memory Match
5) Checkers Lite
6) Minesweeper
7) Mini Sudoku (4×4)
8) Conway’s Game of Life (5×5)
9) Rock–Paper–Scissors
10) Coin Flip
11) Guess the Number
12) Dice Duel
13) Battleships
14) Hangman
15) 2048 (Text)
16) Dungeon Crawl (Rogue-lite)
17) Word Chain
18) 20 Questions
19) Sentence Builder
20) Advanced Story Engine

X) Exit

- Ask: “Which game do you want to play? (type the number, or X to exit)”
- When the user chooses a game, switch to that game’s engine.
- Let the user type `MENU` at any time to return to this main menu.
- Let the user type `RESTART` to restart the current game from scratch.
- Let the user type `HELP` to briefly restate the rules of the current game.

0.4 HIDDEN STATE & FAIR PLAY (ANTI-CHEAT PROTOCOL)
You MUST follow all of these rules in every game:

1) HIDDEN STATE COMMITMENT
   - If the game requires hidden information (bomb locations, secret numbers, face-down cards, AI ship placement, etc.), 
     you:
     - Generate that hidden information once at setup.
     - Internally commit to it and never change it unless rules explicitly say so.
   - You NEVER retroactively alter hidden state to make the game “interesting” or to help or hurt the player.

2) PUBLIC VS. PRIVATE INFORMATION
   - PUBLIC information: anything printed in chat (boards, revealed tiles/cards, hit/miss markers, scores, guesses already made).
   - HIDDEN information: anything the player should not know yet (bomb locations, unrevealed cards, AI ship placement, chosen secret word, etc.).
   - When choosing the AI’s actions in **imperfect information** situations:
     - Make decisions using ONLY the public information, not the hidden state.
     - After choosing an action, then consult the hidden state to determine the outcome (hit/miss, correct/incorrect, etc.).
   - Example: Battleships AI:
     - First choose a coordinate based only on previous hits/misses the player can see.
     - Only after choosing do you check the hidden AI board or the player’s hidden board to see if it is a hit.

3) RANDOMNESS
   - For required “random” decisions (e.g. Rock–Paper–Scissors, coin flips, AI ship placement, bomb placement, memory card layout, etc.):
     - Behave as if you choose uniformly at random.
     - Do not bias toward helping or hurting the player unless game rules explicitly say so.

4) NO PERFECT FORESIGHT
   - The AI must not act as if it knows future user choices.
   - The AI must not act as if it knows hidden user thoughts (e.g. what number they are thinking of).
   - If you need to “guess” something the user is secretly thinking of, treat it as a fair guess based on probabilities and clues.

5) CONSISTENCY
   - Once a board, layout, or secret is created, it must stay consistent across all future turns.
   - If you ever detect that you’ve contradicted a previous board or rule, immediately:
     - Acknowledge the inconsistency.
     - Fix the current board/state so it is consistent with what was previously shown.
     - Continue from the corrected state.

========================================
1. GAME MODULES
========================================

When a game is active, you obey that game’s specific rules in addition to the global rules above.

For every game:
- Always clearly show the full board or current state after each move (if applicable).
- Keep track of turns, scores, win/lose/draw conditions.
- Clearly announce when the game ends and offer:
  - `RESTART` the same game
  - `MENU` to return to GameHub

----------------------------------------
1.1 Tic-Tac-Toe (3×3)
----------------------------------------
- Symbols:
  - Empty: “⬜”
  - Player: “❌”
  - AI: “⭕”
- Board: 3×3 grid.
- At start:
  - Show an empty grid.
  - Make the AI’s first move as “⭕”.
- After each move:
  - Show the full 3×3 grid.
  - Indicate whose turn it is and prompt for the player’s move (e.g. coordinate system).
- Win condition:
  - First to 3 in a row (horizontal, vertical, diagonal).
- End:
  - Announce winner or draw.
  - Offer `RESTART` or `MENU`.

----------------------------------------
1.2 Connect Four (7×6)
----------------------------------------
- Symbols:
  - Empty: “⚪”
  - Player: “🔴”
  - AI: “🟡”
- Grid: 7 columns × 6 rows.
- Under the grid, always print:
  1 2 3 4 5 6 7
- At start:
  - Show empty grid.
  - Make the AI’s first move (drop “🟡” into a column).
- On each turn:
  - Player chooses column 1–7.
  - Drop piece into lowest available cell in that column.
  - Show full grid after every move.
- Win condition:
  - 4 in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
- End:
  - Announce winner or draw.
  - Offer `RESTART` or `MENU`.

----------------------------------------
1.3 Gomoku (Five in a Row, 9×9)
----------------------------------------
- Symbols:
  - Empty: “⬜”
  - Player: “❌”
  - AI: “⭕”
- Grid: 9×9.
- Label columns with numbers (1–9).
- Label rows with capital letters.
- First to 5 in a row wins.
- The AI starts.
- Always show the board after each move.

----------------------------------------
1.4 Memory Match (4×4)
----------------------------------------
- Board: 4×4 cards face-down.
- Hidden state:
  - Randomly assign matching pairs under the 16 positions at the start.
- Display:
  - Face-down cards as “⬜”.
  - When user picks two coordinates, temporarily reveal them and tell if they match.
- Rules:
  - Matching pair → stay revealed, user scores a point.
  - Non-matching → flip back next turn.
- Track score and remaining pairs.

----------------------------------------
1.5 Checkers Lite (4×4)
----------------------------------------
- Board: 4×4.
- Symbols:
  - Empty: “⬜”
  - Player pieces: “⚫”
  - AI pieces: “⚪”
- Turn-based moves, captures are mandatory.
- Define simple move and capture rules.
- Always show board after move.

----------------------------------------
1.6 Minesweeper (5×5)
----------------------------------------
- Grid: 5×5.
- Symbols:
  - Hidden: “□”
  - Bomb: “💣”
  - Revealed numbers: digits for adjacent bomb counts.
- Hidden state:
  - On setup, randomly place exactly 5 bombs in distinct cells once.
  - Do not change bomb placement during game.
- Coordinates:
  - Columns: numbers.
  - Rows: capital letters.
- Player action:
  - Chooses coordinates to uncover.
  - If bomb → game over (reveal entire board).
  - Else → reveal number (0–8) and auto-reveal neighbors if 0 if you want.
- Win:
  - All non-bomb cells revealed.

----------------------------------------
1.7 Mini Sudoku (4×4)
----------------------------------------
- 4×4 Sudoku with digits 1–4.
- Board uses “□” for blanks.
- You and the user cooperate:
  - User fills one number per turn.
  - You check validity and update board.
- Enforce Sudoku constraints.

----------------------------------------
1.8 Conway’s Game of Life (5×5)
----------------------------------------
- Grid: 5×5.
- Symbols:
  - Dead: “⬜”
  - Live: “⬛”
- You simulate generations according to Life rules.
- Show grid each generation.
- Let user control:
  - Initial pattern (or random).
  - When to step to next generation.

----------------------------------------
1.9 Rock–Paper–Scissors
----------------------------------------
- Behavior:
  1) Ask which language to use (respect global language already set; if user wants to change, allow).
  2) Then, in that language, say: 
     “In your mind, choose one: 🪨 📄 ✂️. Type ‘go’ and I’ll reveal mine.”
  3) When the user types “go” (case-insensitive), reply with exactly one of:
     - 🪨
     - 📄
     - ✂️
     chosen uniformly at random.
  4) For any other input, repeat step 2.

----------------------------------------
1.10 Coin Flip
----------------------------------------
- Behavior:
  1) Ask which language to use (reuse or change).
  2) Then say in that language: Tell the user to type "flip" to flip the coin.
  3) Only when the user types "flip" (case-insensitive), reply with exactly one of:
     - “🪙 👤”
     - “🪙 🦅”
     chosen uniformly at random.
  4) For any other input, repeat step 2.

----------------------------------------
1.11 Guess the Number (1–100)
----------------------------------------
- Hidden state:
  - Choose a secret integer between 1 and 100 uniformly at random and commit to it.
- User:
  - Guesses numbers.
- You:
  - Reply “higher”, “lower”, or “correct”.
  - Track number of guesses.
- End:
  - When correct, reveal secret number and attempts.

----------------------------------------
1.12 Dice Duel
----------------------------------------
- Each round:
  - Roll 2 dice for user and 2 for AI (simulate uniformly 1–6).
  - Announce both totals and who wins the round.
  - Keep running score.
- Optionally allow best-of-N or play indefinitely until user stops.

----------------------------------------
1.13 Battleships (10×10)
----------------------------------------
- You are the game engine and narrator for ⚓ Battleships ⚓.

Display & Symbols:
- 🌊 = water
- 🚢 = ship
- 💥 = hit
- ❌ = miss

Boards:
- 10×10 for each side.
- Rows: A–J
- Columns: 1–10
- Always show:
  - Player board (full: ships + hits/misses).
  - AI board (only hits/misses and water; ships hidden).

Welcome Phase:
- Show banner and short intro.
- Immediately proceed to language confirmation (already chosen globally) and then mode:

Mode Selection:
- 1. AI Mode (vs AI)
- 2. Pass & Play (two humans, you just handle state).

Setup:
- Each player has:
  - 1 ship length 4
  - 2 ships length 3
  - 2 ships length 2
- Ships are axis-aligned, within bounds, no overlap.
- For AI ships:
  - Place them randomly and commit to that layout as hidden state.
- Show placement grid after each player placement.
- In Pass & Play, keep both boards hidden appropriately but still track them.

Gameplay Loop:
- Turns alternate.
- Shots are coordinates like “B7”.
- For each shot:
  - Decide the coordinate.
  - THEN check the hidden board to see hit or miss.
- Mark:
  - 💥 for hits.
  - ❌ for misses.
- Keep marks permanent.
- AI Behavior:
  - Use only public hit/miss history for search.
  - Do not target using hidden ship positions directly.
  - Use probabilistic search patterns; may sometimes choose suboptimal moves.

Endgame:
- When all ships of a side are sunk:
  - Announce winner.
  - Reveal both full final boards.
  - Offer `RESTART` or `MENU`.

----------------------------------------
1.14 Hangman (Vislice)
----------------------------------------
- Hidden state:
  - Choose a secret word and commit to it.
- Display:
  - Masked word (e.g. “_ _ _ _”).
  - Hangman progress (wrong guesses).
- Player:
  - Guesses letters.
- Rules:
  - Correct guesses reveal all instances.
  - Wrong guesses move the hangman closer to completion.
- End:
  - Player wins if word revealed.
  - Player loses if hangman is complete.
  - Reveal word at the end.

----------------------------------------
1.15 2048 (Text, 4×4)
----------------------------------------
- Grid: 4×4 of numbers (powers of 2) and empty cells.
- Represent empty as “·” or “.”.
- At start:
  - Place two tiles (2 or 4) randomly in empty cells.
- Each move:
  - Player chooses direction: up, down, left, right.
  - You:
    - Slide tiles.
    - Merge equal tiles per 2048 rules.
    - Add one new 2 or 4 in a random empty cell.
  - Show full grid.
- End:
  - Player loses if no moves possible.
  - Optionally treat reaching 2048 as “win” but allow play beyond.

----------------------------------------
1.16 Dungeon Crawl (Rogue-lite, 5×5)
----------------------------------------
- Grid: 5×5.
- Symbols:
  - Empty: “⬜”
  - Player: “🧙”
  - Monster: “👾”
  - Treasure: “💎”
  - Exit: “🚪”
- Hidden state:
  - Randomly populate monsters, treasure, exit at start, commit.
- Each turn:
  - Show grid with player position visible.
  - Player chooses move: up, down, left, right.
  - Resolve:
    - If move into 👾 → combat or simple “you lose” depending on difficulty.
    - If move into 💎 → collect treasure, update score/inventory.
    - If move into 🚪 → exit dungeon, game end.
- Keep track of health, treasure, and progress.

----------------------------------------
1.17 Word Chain
----------------------------------------
- Rules:
  - Start with a word.
  - Next word must start with last letter of previous word.
  - No repeats.
- You and user alternate providing words.
- Track used words to avoid repeats.

----------------------------------------
1.18 20 Questions
----------------------------------------
- Hidden state:
  - You think of an object, person, or concept (secret).
- Player:
  - May ask up to 20 yes/no questions.
- You:
  - Answer honestly with yes/no/maybe.
- Player can attempt guesses at any time.
- End:
  - Player guesses correctly → win.
  - 20 questions used with no correct guess → reveal secret.

----------------------------------------
1.19 Sentence Builder
----------------------------------------
- Collaborative story:
  - You start by giving a setting sentence.
  - Then alternate one sentence at a time with the user.
- Maintain internal consistency of story, but this game has no failure state.

----------------------------------------
1.20 Advanced Story Engine
----------------------------------------
- When the user selects this option, switch into “Advanced Story Engine” mode.
- Then:
  - Apply the full Advanced Story Engine specification you have been given (world bible, missions, lore, skills, reputation, COMMAND BOARD, etc.).
  - Treat it as a separate game module with its own hidden state and complex systems.
- You still respect:
  - Language preference.
  - Player name (can be reused as character name if desired, or ask separately).
- Begin with Step 1 of that system: Request story parameters.

========================================
2. SESSION CONTROL
========================================

At all times:
- Recognize commands:
  - `MENU` → End current game gracefully and show main menu.
  - `RESTART` → Restart current game from scratch.
  - `HELP` → Explain rules and input format of current game.
  - `QUIT` or `EXIT` → Confirm, then end the whole GameHub session.

Remember:
- Never cheat with hidden state.
- Never retroactively change secret information.
- Always keep game behavior consistent with the rules above.

--- END OF PROMPT

entry.title: The emerging 2028 field and America’s continued support for genocide
entry.content:
Twenty-Three Names, Two Exceptions

The emerging 2028 field and America’s continued support for genocide

Political analysis and position note · campaign finance, Gaza, genocide, U.S. foreign policy, democracy, oligarchy, and media power

Andraž Đurič

Version 1 · 17 August 2026

Abstract

Track AIPAC’s early list of potential 2028 presidential candidates contains 23 names: 16 Democrats and seven Republicans. Within that list, 21 are presented as pro-Israel or materially aligned with the pro-Israel lobby. Only two, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Ro Khanna, are presented as rejecting AIPAC and its allies. Fourteen entries display numerical lobby totals. Added together, those displayed figures equal $14,140,376. Nine entries have no comparable federal total.

This is not evidence of a coming choice between two substantially different foreign policies. It is evidence of a political field being assembled around the continuation of an existing one. The relevant money is not politically inert because it is routed through PAC contributions, earmarked contributions, advertising, or nominally independent expenditures. It finances electoral capacity. It rewards alignment, protects incumbents, elevates selected candidates, attacks dissidents, and makes deviation more costly. When financial support converges with voting records, policy platforms, and repeated public statements, heightened skepticism is the rational response.

That alignment matters because the United States is not a distant observer of Gaza. It supplies Israel with billions of dollars in annual military assistance, weapons, maintenance, and diplomatic protection. Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. The conclusion rests not on casualty figures alone, but on the combined pattern of mass killing, severe bodily and mental harm, destruction of the conditions required for life, obstruction of food and water, devastation of medicine and sanitation, forced displacement, confinement, and statements of eliminationist intent.

The emerging 2028 field therefore offers a glimpse of political catastrophe already being normalized: another presidential election in which Americans may be permitted to choose the manager of U.S. support for genocide, but scarcely permitted to vote for ending it.

Epistemic key

Claim type Standing in this article
Tracker-reported Candidate names, classifications, PAC affiliations, and displayed dollar figures come from Track AIPAC’s 17 August 2026 page and stated methodology.
Recomputed The 23-name count, party split, two-exception count, 14 numerical entries, nine missing totals, and $14,140,376 sum were independently recomputed from that page.
Empirical Mortality, U.S. military aid, billionaire spending, media ownership, and political influence claims are tied to peer-reviewed research, official records, or identified research reports.
Legal and analytical conclusion The genocide conclusion is argued here and is also the conclusion of the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry, Amnesty International, and the Israeli human-rights organization B’Tselem. A final ICJ judgment remains pending.
Rate-equivalent The 31–42-year and approximately 76-year figures translate observed death rates into one prewar population-equivalent. They are diagnostics of scale, not demographic forecasts.

1. The early field

The Track AIPAC page is not a ballot and does not claim to be one. It is an early list of plausible contenders. That limitation does not make the pattern uninformative. Presidential fields do not appear fully formed on filing day. They are assembled years in advance through donor networks, media attention, party institutions, endorsements, staffing, polling, and the prior distribution of political legitimacy.

As of 17 August 2026, the list contains 23 people. On the Democratic side it names Andy Beshear, Cory Booker, Pete Buttigieg, Rahm Emanuel, Ruben Gallego, Kamala Harris, Mark Kelly, Ro Khanna, Wes Moore, Gavin Newsom, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Jon Ossoff, JB Pritzker, Josh Shapiro, Elissa Slotkin, and Gretchen Whitmer. On the Republican side it names Ted Cruz, Ron DeSantis, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Kristi Noem, Marco Rubio, JD Vance, and Glenn Youngkin.

Only Ocasio-Cortez and Khanna are presented as rejecting AIPAC and its allies. Khanna is identified as a signer of the PEACE Pledge. Ocasio-Cortez is assigned a lobby total of zero. Every other name is presented in the pro-Israel or lobby-aligned field, whether through an explicit warning, a red scorecard, a financing record, or a documented institutional connection.

Twenty-three possible candidates. Twenty-one aligned with Israel. Two exceptions.

The catastrophe is not merely that many politicians support Israel in some abstract or qualified sense. It is that, after Gaza, support for the state carrying out this destruction remains close to a bipartisan entrance requirement for the presidency.

Metric Value Standing
Potential contenders listed 23 16 Democrats; 7 Republicans
Presented as pro-Israel or lobby-aligned 21 Track AIPAC classification and scorecards
Presented as rejecting AIPAC and allies 2 Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez; Ro Khanna
Entries with numerical totals 14 Includes Ocasio-Cortez at $0
Democratic displayed subtotal $11,955,852 9 entries with numerical totals
Republican displayed subtotal $2,184,524 5 entries with numerical totals
Sum of displayed numerical totals $14,140,376 Arithmetic recomputed from the page
Entries without comparable federal totals 9 Absence of a total is not evidence of absence of influence

2. What the money shows

Track AIPAC describes its figures as federal-career totals drawn from Federal Election Commission data. Its FAQ distinguishes direct and earmarked PAC contributions from independent expenditures such as advertising. Its methodology statement says a financial record alone is not sufficient for its red scorecard. It also evaluates voting records, published policy positions, public statements, and credible reporting about candidates seeking lobby support.

That last point matters. It is false to treat the page as a pile of dollar figures and then dismiss it because dollars alone do not reconstruct a private conversation. The financial and political evidence point in the same direction. These candidates have generally not hidden their support for Israel. In many cases they have repeated it, voted for it, incorporated it into policy, or accepted organized electoral assistance from groups dedicated to preserving it.

Influence need not convert an opponent. It can select, finance, elevate, and protect an ally.

The cartoon model of corruption imagines a hostile politician receiving a bag of cash and immediately reversing a vote. Real political influence is usually more structural. Money pays for staff, data, advertising, opposition research, canvassing, legal work, and access to audiences. It makes some candidacies viable and others impossible. It can overwhelm a primary opponent, deter future challengers, and demonstrate what happens to officeholders who defect.

No secret quid pro quo is required. A lobby can recruit candidates already aligned with it, fund them over competitors, preserve their careers, and punish deviation. The result is a selection environment in which the views of organized wealth become overrepresented before most voters encounter a ballot.

The displayed total of $14,140,376 should be read exactly at its evidentiary strength. It is the sum of the 14 numerical figures shown on the page, not a transaction-by-transaction reconstruction of the entire pro-Israel donor universe. The tracker is an advocacy project, and its methodology pages are not perfectly harmonized about the treatment of large individual donors after its April 2026 reversion to its earlier method. None of that makes the visible financing meaningless. It means the proper conclusion is narrower and stronger: the page documents substantial organized electoral support for a field whose public records overwhelmingly converge on continued support for Israel.

3. What American taxpayers finance

The political alignment has material consequences. Under the current ten-year U.S.-Israel memorandum, the United States committed $38 billion in military support for fiscal years 2019 through 2028: $3.3 billion per year in Foreign Military Financing and $500 million per year for missile-defense cooperation. The structure is documented by the U.S. State Department and the Congressional Research Service.

The baseline understates the post-7 October commitment. A 2025 report co-published by the Quincy Institute and Brown University’s Costs of War Project estimated that the United States provided at least $21.7 billion in military aid to Israel between 7 October 2023 and September 2025, while committing tens of billions more through arms agreements for later delivery or payment.

The subsidy is direct. The causal attribution of one tax dollar to one bomb, one destroyed home, or one dead child may be administratively indirect, but the military relationship is not. U.S. money finances weapons, munitions, aircraft, missile defense, maintenance, spare parts, stock replenishment, domestic Israeli procurement, and the military capacity within which the assault is conducted.

American voters are therefore not being asked to form an opinion about a remote conflict over which their government has no control. Their government supplies the state conducting it. Their representatives authorize the money. Their presidential candidates compete to preserve the relationship.

4. The word is genocide

The Genocide Convention does not require the killing of every member of a protected group. It covers specified acts committed with intent to destroy a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group, in whole or in part. Those acts include killing members of the group, causing serious bodily or mental harm, deliberately inflicting conditions of life calculated to bring about physical destruction, imposing measures intended to prevent births, and forcibly transferring children.

Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. The basis is cumulative:

  • Palestinians have been killed en masse, including an enormous number of civilians and children.
  • Israeli attacks and siege conditions have caused severe bodily and mental harm on a population-wide scale.
  • Homes, hospitals, water systems, sanitation, food production, schools, and other conditions required for collective life have been destroyed or disabled.
  • Food, water, fuel, medicine, and humanitarian relief have been blocked, restricted, or made radically inadequate.
  • Most of the population has been repeatedly displaced within a sealed territory in which meaningful flight has been denied.
  • Senior Israeli political and military figures have made repeated statements that supply evidence of eliminationist intent.
  • Independent foreign reporters have been barred from free access to Gaza, while the Committee to Protect Journalists has recorded extraordinary killing of Palestinian journalists inside it.

This conclusion is not an eccentric use of the word. In September 2025, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry concluded that Israeli authorities and forces had committed four of the five genocidal acts defined in the Convention and that genocidal intent was established from the pattern of conduct and statements by Israeli authorities. Amnesty International reached the genocide conclusion in December 2024. B’Tselem, an Israeli human-rights organization, reached it in July 2025.

Israel denies the charge, states that it targets Hamas rather than Palestinians as a group, and argues that civilian harm results from warfare against an organization embedded in civilian areas. The International Court of Justice case remains pending; an order of 21 May 2026 set further deadlines for written pleadings rather than issuing a final merits judgment.

Those facts identify the procedural state of the case and the defense being offered. They do not suspend ordinary reasoning until the last judicial document appears. A court’s timetable does not erase bodies, restore hospitals, open borders, supply water, or neutralize evidence of intent.

If mass killing, the destruction of civilian life-support systems, forced displacement inside a sealed territory, obstruction of food and water, the devastation of medical care, and public eliminationist rhetoric do not justify the word genocide, then what work is the word supposed to perform?

A concept becomes meaningless not only when applied too freely, but also when withheld from the very pattern it was created to name.

5. The arithmetic of erasure

My earlier report, Casualty Analysis: Direct and Indirect Death Tolls in Gaza vs. Ukraine, reported more than 72,300 named and recorded direct deaths by mid-April 2026. Against a prewar population of roughly 2.2 million, that is about 3.3 percent of the population killed directly in approximately two and a half years.

If the recorded absolute rate were held mechanically constant, with births, migration, changing military intensity, and every other demographic process ignored, one prewar Gaza population-equivalent would be killed in roughly:

2,200,000 ÷ (72,300 ÷ 2.5) ≈ 76 years.

That is the conservative, confirmed-record translation: less than a century.

A stronger mortality study supports the shorter range without relying on speculative multipliers. A 2026 peer-reviewed, population-representative field survey in The Lancet Global Health estimated 75,200 violent deaths between 7 October 2023 and 5 January 2025, with a 95 percent confidence interval of 63,600 to 86,800. The central estimate was approximately 3.4 percent of Gaza’s pre-conflict population killed violently in about 15 months. It also estimated 16,300 non-violent deaths, including 8,540 deaths above the pre-conflict projection.

Translating only the violent-death proportion into a fixed-rate population-equivalent gives:

3.4% in 15 months → about 2.72% per year → about 36.8 years per prewar population-equivalent.

Using the rounded 3 to 4 percent survey range yields approximately 31 to 42 years. This is the three-to-four-decade figure. It is not a guess. It is a transparent transformation of a peer-reviewed mortality estimate produced through a population-representative field survey.

These calculations are deliberately called rate-equivalents, not forecasts. They do not predict that the rate will remain fixed, that no Palestinians will be born, that no one will flee, or that history proceeds linearly. Nor does genocide require killing everyone. The calculation performs a simpler moral and epistemic function: it converts percentages that can be psychologically minimized into a timescale commensurate with the destruction already measured.

Under the conservative named-record rate, the answer is under 100 years. Under the peer-reviewed survey rate, it is roughly three to four decades. A political system preparing to continue material support for that process is not confronting an ambiguous abstraction. It is choosing what rate of Palestinian erasure it is willing to finance.

6. Idiocracy inside oligarchy

American electoral failure cannot be explained by voter ignorance alone, but voter ignorance cannot be omitted. A democracy without a scientifically literate, historically literate, epistemologically literate population trained in critical thinking is vulnerable to propaganda, tribal identity, motivated reasoning, fabricated certainty, and the repetition of catastrophic choices. In that sense, the repeated idiocy of American electoral behavior can be called an idiocracy.

But it is also an oligarchy. The population does not select from an unfiltered field, deliberate within a neutral information environment, or possess equal power to make its preferences politically real. Wealth decides which candidates can become visible, which messages can be repeated at scale, which institutions survive, and which deviations become professionally dangerous.

The numbers are not subtle. Americans for Tax Fairness calculated that just 100 billionaire families spent $2.6 billion in the 2024 federal elections, about one dollar in six of total candidate, party, and committee spending. Seventy percent of their money supported Republican candidates and conservative causes; 23 percent supported Democrats and progressive causes. More than 80 percent flowed through super PACs and hybrid PACs. A Roosevelt Institute synthesis reports that nearly three-quarters of billionaire spending in the presidential race supported Donald Trump. The Brennan Center documents how megadonor-funded outside groups assumed core campaign functions and placed a tiny group of wealthy donors at the center of the 2024 election.

Peer-reviewed political science points in the same structural direction. Martin Gilens and Benjamin Page analyzed 1,779 policy issues and found that economic elites and business-oriented organized groups had substantial independent effects on U.S. policy, while average citizens and mass-based groups had little or no independent influence after the other actors’ preferences were taken into account. Their dataset covers 1981 through 2002 and is not the last word on every institution or era. It is nevertheless direct evidence against the comforting myth that American policy is simply the unmediated will of an equal citizenry.

The information environment is also concentrated. Free Press describes a small cartel of billionaires, private-equity firms, and conglomerates controlling much of what Americans see, read, and hear. A 2026 FAIR ownership analysis counted 45.6 billion visits to the 50 largest U.S. news websites from December 2024 through November 2025; nearly 25.5 billion, more than half, went to sites controlled by only seven families or corporate entities.

Billionaires disproportionately finance the far right. Billionaires and conglomerates also own large parts of the media through which the public perceives candidates, war, protest, legitimacy, and the boundaries of allegedly serious opinion. The same class can therefore influence both the menu and the story told about the menu.

Idiocracy describes a recurring electoral output. Oligarchy describes the structure that filters the candidates, finances the viable choices, and concentrates the machinery of public perception.

The two systems are not opposites. They reinforce each other. Low public epistemic capacity makes oligarchic manipulation easier. Oligarchic control of politics and media makes the cultivation of genuine public epistemic capacity less likely. Formal voting then supplies democratic authorization to outcomes that concentrated wealth did disproportionate work to construct.

7. What 2028 threatens to reproduce

It is too early to know which of the 23 people on this page will run, survive a primary, or reach the general election. It is not too early to recognize the boundary being drawn around acceptable power. If 21 of 23 plausible candidates are already aligned in some form with continued support for Israel, then the nominal variety of names conceals a severe restriction in policy choice.

Historians will presumably see this period more clearly than we can while living through it. But I am certain they will look back in horror at a country that proclaimed itself the greatest in the world, posed for generations as the world’s protector, and then revealed itself as its most powerful bully.

They will also study it as a demonstration that idiocracy and oligarchy can coexist and reinforce one another. American voters repeatedly elevate catastrophic leaders, but they do not choose from an unfiltered field or within a neutral information environment. Billionaires finance politicians and super PACs, disproportionately fund the far right, and, together with a small number of conglomerates and private-equity firms, control much of the media through which the population perceives reality.

A democracy without a scientifically, historically, and epistemologically literate population trained in critical thinking cannot reliably resist this capture. It can instead become the mechanism through which oligarchic power manufactures public consent and acquires democratic authorization, with consequences catastrophic far beyond the country’s borders.

The prospective 2028 field is one such consequence. The choice being prepared is not whether American money should continue sustaining the military capacity of a state committing genocide. The choice is increasingly who will administer that support, narrate it as virtue, and punish those who refuse the premise.

America is not merely failing to stop a genocide. It is financing the state committing it and preparing another presidential election in which ending that support may scarcely exist as an option.

Standing and limits

This is a political analysis and position note, not a prediction of the final 2028 ballot. The candidate list is a dated snapshot from an advocacy tracker. “Pro-Israel” covers different degrees and forms of alignment and does not establish that every listed person endorses every act of the Israeli government. Candidate positions can change.

The $14,140,376 total is reproducible arithmetic from displayed page figures. It is not represented as a complete audit of every relevant FEC transaction or as proof of a private bargain. The inference is structural: organized finance materially supports candidates; public records overwhelmingly indicate aligned positions; and money can exert influence by selection, amplification, protection, and punishment without purchasing a sudden reversal.

The genocide conclusion is stated without euphemism. A final ICJ merits judgment is pending, but legal procedure is not the only permissible form of justified belief. The conclusion is supported by the documented conduct, the Genocide Convention’s elements, and convergent findings by independent international and Israeli organizations.

The erasure figures are rate-equivalents. They answer what timescale follows if a measured rate is translated into one prewar population-equivalent. They do not claim a stable future rate or literal demographic extinction on a scheduled date. Their purpose is to make the magnitude of existing mortality harder to hide behind innumeracy.

References

  1. Track AIPAC, “2028 Presidential Candidates”, accessed 17 August 2026.
  2. Track AIPAC, “Track AIPAC Adapting Data Methodology to Identify the Israel Lobby’s Hidden Donor Movements”, 27 March 2026, updated 28 April 2026.
  3. Track AIPAC, “Frequently Asked Questions”, accessed 17 August 2026.
  4. U.S. Department of State, “Ten-Year Memorandum of Understanding Between the United States and Israel”, 14 September 2016.
  5. Jeremy M. Sharp, U.S. Foreign Aid to Israel: Overview and Developments since October 7, 2023, Congressional Research Service Report RL33222, updated 28 May 2025.
  6. William D. Hartung, “U.S. Military Aid and Arms Transfers to Israel, October 2023–September 2025”, Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft and Brown University Costs of War Project, 7 October 2025.
  7. United Nations, Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, adopted 9 December 1948, especially Article II.
  8. UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel, Legal Analysis of the Conduct of Israel in Gaza Pursuant to the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, A/HRC/60/CRP.3, 16 September 2025; see also the official findings summary.
  9. Amnesty International, “You Feel Like You Are Subhuman”: Israel’s Genocide Against Palestinians in Gaza, MDE 15/8668/2024, 5 December 2024.
  10. B’Tselem, Our Genocide, July 2025.
  11. State of Israel, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, “MFA Statement Following the ICJ Decision on Provisional Measures”, 26 January 2024.

Michael Spagat, Jon Pedersen, Khalil Shikaki, Michael Robbins, Eran Bendavid, Håvard Hegre, and Debarati Guha-Sapir, “Violent and Non-Violent Death Tolls for the Gaza Conflict: New Primary Evidence from a Population-Representative Field Survey”, The Lancet Global Health 14, no. 4 (2026), e552–e559; PubMed record.
  14. Andraž Đurič, “Casualty Analysis: Direct and Indirect Death Tolls in Gaza vs. Ukraine (April 2026)”, Epistemic Forge, 17 April 2026.

  17. Marina Pino and Julia Fishman, “Fifteen Years Later, Citizens United Defined the 2024 Election”, Brennan Center for Justice, 14 January 2025.
